Every year the [American Kennel Club](http://akc.org/) releases our ranking of the most popular dog breeds based on AKC registration statistics for the previous year.

The [French Bulldog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/french-bulldog/) continues to top the rankings at the No. 1 spot for the fourth year in a row. The [Labrador Retriever](https://www.akc.org/press-releases/labrador-retriever-celebrates-30-years-top-spot-french-bulldog-overtakes-german-shepherd-dog-number-2-spot/), who had a 31-year run as the most popular breed, is in the No. 2 spot for the third year in a row. In 2025, the Poodle moved out of the top five, replaced by the [Dachshund](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/dachshund/). Many other breeds have moved spots from 2024 to 2025. Below, find ranked annual lists of [AKC-recognized breeds](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/).

    4.   [German Shepherd Dog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-shepherd-dog/)
    5.   Dachshund

Every year the [American Kennel Club](http://akc.org/) releases our ranking of the most popular dog breeds based on AKC registration statistics for the previous year.

The [French Bulldog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/french-bulldog/) continues to top the rankings at the No. 1 spot for the fourth year in a row. The [Labrador Retriever](https://www.akc.org/press-releases/labrador-retriever-celebrates-30-years-top-spot-french-bulldog-overtakes-german-shepherd-dog-number-2-spot/), who had a 31-year run as the most popular breed, is in the No. 2 spot for the third year in a row. In 2025, the Poodle moved out of the top five, replaced by the [Dachshund](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/dachshund/). Many other breeds have moved spots from 2024 to 2025. Below, find ranked annual lists of [AKC-recognized breeds](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/).

    1.   French Bulldog
    2.   Labrador Retriever

    4.   [German Shepherd Dog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-shepherd-dog/)
    5.   Dachshund

As the world’s largest registry of purebred dogs, the AKC uses our registration statistics to rank the most popular breeds of the past year — and the numbers are in!

The [French Bulldog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/french-bulldog/) has secured the No. 1 spot as the most popular dog breed in the United States for the third year in a row. In 2022, the Frenchie took the Most Popular title from the [Labrador Retriever,](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/labrador-retriever/) a breed who had previously sat comfortably at [No. 1 for 31 years](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/most-popular-dog-breeds-of-2021/).

## Staying in the No.1 Spot

French Bulldogs have surged to the top, quickly amassing popularity for their size and adaptability. It’s hard to miss their signature bat ears on city streets and rural roads alike.

Over the last 12 years, they’ve climbed the rankings. In 2012, they were ranked the No. 14 most popular breed, and by 2021, they’d made it to the No. 2 spot. They officially became the [No.1 breed in 2022](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/most-popular-dog-breeds-2022/), and have held that title for three years now.

French Bulldogs are especially popular in cities, but their playful nature and compact size are great for a variety of lifestyles. These little dogs originated in France, and [French Bulldog history](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/breed-history-french-bulldog/) is complex. They were recognized by the American Kennel Club in 1898, and now have over 100 years of AKC history behind them.

## Top 10 Dog Breeds of 2024

The top five and top 10 dog breeds are popular for a reason, and typically don’t shift too much. The Frenchie is again at No. 1, followed by the Labrador Retriever, [Golden Retriever](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/golden-retriever/), [German Shepherd Dog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-shepherd-dog/), and [Poodle](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/poodle-standard/) at No. 5.

As for the rest of the top 10, a few placements have shifted. [Beagles](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/beagle/) have moved from No. 8 to No. 7, moving [Bulldogs](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bulldog/) from No. 7 to No. 9 and [Rottweilers](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/rottweiler/) from No. 9 to No. 8. [German Shorthaired Pointers](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-shorthaired-pointer/) remain at No. 10 from 2023 to 2024.

## Big Shifts of Note in 2024

2024 saw major shifts for a lot of breeds across the rankings. While some breeds surged over 20 rankings higher, others shifted 10 or more rankings lower. Many breeds, especially in the 20s and 30s, stayed at the same spot from 2023 to 2024.

The [Danish-Swedish Farmdog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/danish-swedish-farmdog/), which [debuted in January 2025](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/danish-swedish-farmdog-newest-akc-recognized-breed/) as part of the [Working Group](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/working/) as the 202nd AKC-recognized breed will be included in the registration rankings for 2025. The Lancashire Heeler, which became AKC-recognized in January 2024, debuted in the 2024 rankings at No. 189.

### Climbing the Rankings

The biggest surges in popularity among breeds came from four very different dog breeds. The [Bracco Italiano](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bracco-italiano/), [recognized by the AKC in 2022](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/bracco-italiano-becomes-newest-akc-recognized-dog-breed-in-2022/), continues to move up. From 2023 to 2024, the Bracco moved up 20 spots from No. 152 to No. 132.

## Least Popular Dog Breeds of 2024

Often rare breeds, the dogs in the bottom 20 have the lowest numbers in terms of registration in the United States. There are 201 breeds counted since the addition of the [Lancashire Heeler](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/lancashire-heeler/) in 2024, and there will be 202 for 2025 when the registration numbers for the Danish-Swedish Farmdog are added.

The [Sloughi](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/sloughi/), which was ranked last at No. 200 in 2023, has made the jump to No. 197 in 2024. They’re followed by the [Norwegian Lundehund](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/lancashire-heeler/) at No. 198, the [Grand Basset Griffon Vendeen](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/grand-basset-griffon-vendeen/) at No. 199, the [Bergamasco Sheepdog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bergamasco-sheepdog/) at No. 200, and the [English Foxhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/english-foxhound/) at No. 201. The English Foxhound was ranked 199 in 2023, and dropped two spots in 2024.

As the world’s largest registry of purebred dogs, the AKC uses our registration statistics to rank the most popular breeds of the past year — and the numbers are in!

The [French Bulldog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/french-bulldog/) has secured the No. 1 spot as the most popular dog breed in the United States for the third year in a row. In 2022, the Frenchie took the Most Popular title from the [Labrador Retriever,](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/labrador-retriever/) a breed who had previously sat comfortably at [No. 1 for 31 years](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/most-popular-dog-breeds-of-2021/).

## Staying in the No.1 Spot

French Bulldogs have surged to the top, quickly amassing popularity for their size and adaptability. It’s hard to miss their signature bat ears on city streets and rural roads alike.

Over the last 12 years, they’ve climbed the rankings. In 2012, they were ranked the No. 14 most popular breed, and by 2021, they’d made it to the No. 2 spot. They officially became the [No.1 breed in 2022](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/most-popular-dog-breeds-2022/), and have held that title for three years now.

French Bulldogs are especially popular in cities, but their playful nature and compact size are great for a variety of lifestyles. These little dogs originated in France, and [French Bulldog history](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/breed-history-french-bulldog/) is complex. They were recognized by the American Kennel Club in 1898, and now have over 100 years of AKC history behind them.

![Image 104: French Bulldog giving a kiss to another French Bulldog on the couch.](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/12/French-Bulldog-giving-a-kiss-to-another-French-Bulldog-on-the-couch.jpg)

©fotosmile777 - stock.adobe.com

## Top 10 Dog Breeds of 2024

The top five and top 10 dog breeds are popular for a reason, and typically don’t shift too much. The Frenchie is again at No. 1, followed by the Labrador Retriever, [Golden Retriever](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/golden-retriever/), [German Shepherd Dog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-shepherd-dog/), and [Poodle](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/poodle-standard/) at No. 5.

As for the rest of the top 10, a few placements have shifted. [Beagles](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/beagle/) have moved from No. 8 to No. 7, moving [Bulldogs](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bulldog/) from No. 7 to No. 9 and [Rottweilers](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/rottweiler/) from No. 9 to No. 8. [German Shorthaired Pointers](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-shorthaired-pointer/) remain at No. 10 from 2023 to 2024.

## Big Shifts of Note in 2024

2024 saw major shifts for a lot of breeds across the rankings. While some breeds surged over 20 rankings higher, others shifted 10 or more rankings lower. Many breeds, especially in the 20s and 30s, stayed at the same spot from 2023 to 2024.

The [Danish-Swedish Farmdog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/danish-swedish-farmdog/), which [debuted in January 2025](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/danish-swedish-farmdog-newest-akc-recognized-breed/) as part of the [Working Group](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/working/) as the 202nd AKC-recognized breed will be included in the registration rankings for 2025. The Lancashire Heeler, which became AKC-recognized in January 2024, debuted in the 2024 rankings at No. 189.

![Image 106: English Foxhound standing in a field with a pack.](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/themes/akc/component-library/assets/img/1x1.trans.gif)

Kewalin Madsen/Shutterstock

### Climbing the Rankings

The biggest surges in popularity among breeds came from four very different dog breeds. The [Kerry Blue Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/kerry-blue-terrier/) had the highest jump, moving up a whopping 25 spots from No. 160 to No. 135. The [Bracco Italiano](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bracco-italiano/), [recognized by the AKC in 2022](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/bracco-italiano-becomes-newest-akc-recognized-dog-breed-in-2022/), continues to move up. From 2023 to 2024, the Bracco moved up 20 spots from No. 152 to No. 132.

The [German Pinscher](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-pinscher/) and the [American Staffordshire Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/american-staffordshire-terrier/) both went up 18 spots year over year. The German Pinscher moved from No. 151 to No. 133, and the AmStaff moved from No. 95 to No. 77.

The [Bedlington Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bedlington-terrier/) went up 15 ranks from No. 149 to No. 134, and the[Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/nova-scotia-duck-tolling-retriever/) went up 14 rankings from No. 83 to No. 69.

The [Brussels Griffon](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/brussels-griffon/), [American Eskimo Dog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/american-eskimo-dog/), and [Harrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/harrier/) all went up 13 placements. The Brussels Griffon moved from No. 92 to No. 84, the Eskie from No. 129 to No. 116, and the Harrier from No. 190 to No. 183.

The [Mudi](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/mudi/), [recognized in 2022](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/mudi-becomes-newest-akc-recognized-dog-breed-in-2022/), continues to climb the ranks, going up 12 from No. 130 in 2023 to No. 122 in 2024. The [Polish Lowland Sheepdog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/polish-lowland-sheepdog/) also went up 12 spots, from No. 193 to No. 181.

The [Manchester Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/manchester-terrier-standard/) went up 11 ranks from No. 126 to No. 115, and the [Boykin Spaniel](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/boykin-spaniel/) went up 10 rankings from No. 75 to No. 65.

### Moving Down on the List

![Image 108: English Foxhound standing in a field with a pack.](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/themes/akc/component-library/assets/img/1x1.trans.gif)

©Angel Sallade Photog - stock.adobe.com

The [Saluki](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/saluki/), [Black and Tan Coonhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/black-and-tan-coonhound/), and [Wirehaired Vizsla](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/wirehaired-vizsla/) all saw their breeds move down the list significantly from 2023 to 2024. The Saluki went from No. 120 to No. 141, down 21 spots. The Black and Tan Coonhound went down 20 spots, from No. 131 to No. 151. Down 17 from 2023 to 2024, the Wirehaired Vizsla went from the No. 142 spot to No. 159.

The [Chinese Shar-Pei](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/chinese-shar-pei/) went from No. 70 to No. 83, down 13 spots. Also down 13 spots was the [Field Spaniel](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/field-spaniel/), from No. 147 to No. 160.

Each down 12 spots were the [Bergamasco Sheepdog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bergamasco-sheepdog/), the [Old English Sheepdog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/old-english-sheepdog/), and the [Dogue de Bordeaux](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/dogue-de-bordeaux/). They went from No. 188 to No. 200, No. 77 to No. 89, and No. 84 to No. 96 respectfully.

Other big dogs have moved down as well. The [Neapolitan Mastiff](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/neapolitan-mastiff/) and [Great Pyrenees](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/great-pyrenees/) are both down 10 spots. The Neapolitan Mastiff went from No. 118 to No. 128, and the Pyr went from No. 64 to No. 74.

### Holding Their Spots

These breeds found solace in their 2023 placements and stayed there. The top five breeds stayed the same, but so did the [Shih Tzu](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/shih-tzu/) at No. 20, [Pomeranian](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/pomeranian/) at No. 22, [Boston Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/boston-terrier/) at No. 23, and [Havanese](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/havanese/) at No. 25. In the 30s, [Belgian Malinois](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/belgian-malinois/) stayed at No. 33, [Basset Hounds](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/basset-hound/) stayed at No. 34, [Vizsla](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/vizsla/) stayed at No. 35, and the [Maltese](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/maltese/) stayed at No. 37. The [German Wirehaired Pointer](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-wirehaired-pointer/) stayed at No. 61, and the [Chow Chow](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/chow-chow/) stayed at No. 88. The [Finnish Spitz](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/finnish-spitz/) kept their spot at No. 194.

## Least Popular Dog Breeds of 2024

Often rare breeds, the dogs in the bottom 20 have the lowest numbers in terms of registration in the United States. There are 201 breeds counted since the addition of the [Lancashire Heeler](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/lancashire-heeler/) in 2024, and there will be 202 for 2025 when the registration numbers for the Danish-Swedish Farmdog are added.

The [Sloughi](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/sloughi/), which was ranked last at No. 200 in 2023, has made the jump to No. 197 in 2024. They’re followed by the [Norwegian Lundehund](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/lancashire-heeler/) at No. 198, the [Grand Basset Griffon Vendeen](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/grand-basset-griffon-vendeen/) at No. 199, the [Bergamasco Sheepdog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bergamasco-sheepdog/) at No. 200, and the [English Foxhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/english-foxhound/) at No. 201. The English Foxhound was ranked 199 in 2023, and dropped two spots in 2024.

The American Kennel Club, the world’s largest registry of purebred dogs, uses registration statistics to rank the most popular breeds of the past year. The results for 2025 are in — the [French Bulldog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/french-bulldog/) takes the No. 1 spot once again!

2025 marks the fourth year in a row that the French Bulldog has been able to remain in the top spot. In 2022, they overthrew the [Labrador Retriever](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/labrador-retriever/)‘s [31-year reign](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/most-popular-dog-breeds-of-2021/) in the number one spot, where they’d been since the 1990s. But don’t worry — Labs are still amongst the most popular breeds in the United States.

![Image 104: Young woman sitting in the grass holding her French Bulldog.](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Young-woman-sitting-in-the-grass-holding-her-French-Bulldog.jpg)

Akarawut - stock.adobe.com

The American Kennel Club has recognized 205 breeds since it was first founded in 1884, 202 of which will were counted in the 2025 registration statistics. Three new breeds were recognized in 2026, and will debut in the 2026 registration statistics. Additional breeds are working their way towards recognition through the [AKC Foundation Stock Service](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/foundation-stock-service/) (FSS) and the [Miscellaneous Class](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/miscellaneous-class/). If you’re looking for a puppy of your own, [AKC Marketplace](https://marketplace.akc.org/)can connect you with a responsible breeder.

Knowing your dog will be counted as part of the compilation of the annual breed popularity list is only a small benefit of dog registration. The AKC is the only purebred dog registry in the United States that maintains systematic inspections and investigations. The AKC conducts thousands of inspections each year to ensure compliance with standards that support the welfare, safety, and health of dogs across the nation.

Read on to see the major shifts in popularity, and see where your favorite breed lands!

## The Frenchie Is Four-midable

French Bulldogs have quickly gained popularity over the last decade due to their size and adaptability. They work well in cities and apartments, allowing people with small spaces to have a dog as well.

In 2012, the Frenchie was ranked No. 14 most popular breed, and by 2021, they moved all the way up to the No. 2 spot. [In 2022, they officially moved up](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/most-popular-dog-breeds-2022/) past the Labrador Retriever to take the spot of the Most Popular Breed — a title they’ve held onto for the past four years.

These little dogs hail from France, and [French Bulldog history](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/breed-history-french-bulldog/) is complex. They were recognized by the American Kennel Club in 1898, putting over 100 years of AKC history behind them — and plenty more to come.

The German Shorthaired Pointer and the Bulldog also switched places from 2024 to 2025. The Bulldog was No. 9 in 2024 and moved to No. 10 for 2025. The GSP did the opposite, rising from No. 10 in 2024 to No. 9 in 2025.

## Big Shifts of Popularity for 2025

With 202 breeds in the rankings, 2025 saw some major shifts in breed popularity. Some breeds saw climbs of nearly 30 spots, while others fell in popularity by the same amount. It’s important to note that while some breeds move down in the rankings, it may not mean that they’ve become less popular — it may just mean that another breed has become more popular and moved up.

Some breeds also stayed in the exact same spot, which in most cases means the rankings shifted around it in a way that kept it in the same spot. For example, one breed may be at No. 30 year-over-year, but that could mean that one breed moved up in popularity while another moved down, cancelling out any obvious movement for certain breeds.

### Climbing the Rankings

Some breeds that gained momentum from 2024 to 2025 were working breeds and hunting breeds. The [Bergamasco Sheepdog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bergamasco-sheepdog/), though still towards the bottom of the rankings, went from No. 200 to No. 183, a 17-spot jump. The [English Foxhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/english-foxhound/) and the [Black and Tan Coonhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/black-and-tan-coonhound/) were both up 14 spots, from No. 201 to 187 and No. 151 to 137, respectively. The [English Toy Spaniel](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/english-toy-spaniel/), [Irish Setter](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/irish-setter/), and [Field Spaniel](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/field-spaniel/) all went up 12 spots in the rankings, and the [Greater Swiss Mountain Dog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/greater-swiss-mountain-dog/) and [Norwegian Buhund](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/norwegian-buhund/) were up 11. The [Pointer](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/pointer/) was up 10 spots from No. 121 to 111, and the [Treeing Walker Coonhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/treeing-walker-coonhound/), [Neapolitan Mastiff](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/neapolitan-mastiff/), and [Scottish Deerhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/scottish-deerhound/) were up nine spots from 2024.

The [Wirehaired Viszla](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/wirehaired-vizsla/) saw the highest surge in rankings, going from No. 159 to No. 130, a total of 29 spots. Other notable movements, though smaller, could be attributed to recent trends: the [Giant Schnauzer](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/giant-schnauzer/), which won the AKC National Championship in 2024 and Westminster Best in Show in 2025, saw an increase of five spots from No. 57 to 52.

Other notable jumps include the [American Hairless Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/american-hairless-terrier/), up 17 spots from 125 to 108, and the [Russell Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/russell-terrier/), up 6 from No. 66 to No. 60. The [Otterhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/otterhound/) and [Cirneco dell’Etna](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/cirneco-delletna/), both [rare breeds](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/rarest-dog-breeds-2025/), both moved up seven spots in the rankings, from No. 196 to No. 189 and No. 191 to No. 184. The [Cane Corso](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/cane-corso/) has also been making its way up the rankings over the past few years, rising from No. 14 in 2024 to No. 11 to 2025, nearly breaking into the top 10. [Border Collies](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/border-collie/) rose four spots in the rankings from No. 30 to No. 26, and [Pomeranians](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/pomeranian/) moved up three spots from No. 22 to No. 19.

Similar to climbs in the rankings, shifts down don’t always mean a breed becomes less popular than the year prior. The biggest shifts in rankings were the [Greyhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/greyhound/), down 33 from No. 188 to No. 151, and the [Briard](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/briard/) and [Black Russian Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/black-russian-terrier/), both down 27 spots from 2024. The [Kerry Blue Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/kerry-blue-terrier/), which rose 25 spots from No. 160 to No. 135 in 2024, went to No. 155 in 2025, down 20 spots.

## New Faces for 2025

The [Danish-Swedish Farmdog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/danish-swedish-farmdog/)[debuted in January 2025](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/danish-swedish-farmdog-newest-akc-recognized-breed/) as a member of the [Working Group](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/working/) — the 202nd AKC-recognized breed. The DSF was included in the rankings for the first time in 2025, debuting at No. 170. The [Lancashire Heeler](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/lancashire-heeler/), which was recognized in January 2024, debuted at No. 189 and moved to No. 190 in 2025.

In January 2026, three new dog breeds were recognized: the [Russian Tsvetnaya Bolonka](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/russian-tsvetnaya-bolonka/), the [Teddy Roosevelt Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/teddy-roosevelt-terrier/), and the [Basset Fauve de Bretagne](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/basset-fauve-de-bretagne/). These three breeds will debut in the 2026 rankings, bringing the total number of AKC-registered breeds to 205.

The American Kennel Club, the world’s largest registry of purebred dogs, uses registration statistics to rank the most popular breeds of the past year. The results for 2025 are in — the [French Bulldog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/french-bulldog/) takes the No. 1 spot once again!

2025 marks the fourth year in a row that the French Bulldog has been able to remain in the top spot. In 2022, they overthrew the [Labrador Retriever](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/labrador-retriever/)‘s [31-year reign](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/most-popular-dog-breeds-of-2021/) in the number one spot, where they’d been since the 1990s. But don’t worry — Labs are still amongst the most popular breeds in the United States.

![Image 104: Young woman sitting in the grass holding her French Bulldog.](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Young-woman-sitting-in-the-grass-holding-her-French-Bulldog.jpg)

Akarawut - stock.adobe.com

The American Kennel Club has recognized 205 breeds since it was first founded in 1884, 202 of which will were counted in the 2025 registration statistics. Three new breeds were recognized in 2026, and will debut in the 2026 registration statistics. Additional breeds are working their way towards recognition through the [AKC Foundation Stock Service](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/foundation-stock-service/) (FSS) and the [Miscellaneous Class](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/miscellaneous-class/). If you’re looking for a puppy of your own, [AKC Marketplace](https://marketplace.akc.org/)can connect you with a responsible breeder.

Knowing your dog will be counted as part of the compilation of the annual breed popularity list is only a small benefit of dog registration. The AKC is the only purebred dog registry in the United States that maintains systematic inspections and investigations. The AKC conducts thousands of inspections each year to ensure compliance with standards that support the welfare, safety, and health of dogs across the nation.

Read on to see the major shifts in popularity, and see where your favorite breed lands!

## The Frenchie Is Four-midable

French Bulldogs have quickly gained popularity over the last decade due to their size and adaptability. They work well in cities and apartments, allowing people with small spaces to have a dog as well.

In 2012, the Frenchie was ranked No. 14 most popular breed, and by 2021, they moved all the way up to the No. 2 spot. [In 2022, they officially moved up](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/most-popular-dog-breeds-2022/) past the Labrador Retriever to take the spot of the Most Popular Breed — a title they’ve held onto for the past four years.

These little dogs hail from France, and [French Bulldog history](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/breed-history-french-bulldog/) is complex. They were recognized by the American Kennel Club in 1898, putting over 100 years of AKC history behind them — and plenty more to come.

## Top 10 Dog Breeds of 2025

The top 10 dog breeds are popular for a reason, and typically don’t shift too much. This year, the top five did see a shift: the [Dachshund](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/dachshund/) moved up in popularity from No. 6 to No. 5, pushing the [Poodle](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/poodle-standard/) out of the top five most popular dog breeds.

1.   French Bulldog
2.   Labrador Retriever
3.   [Golden Retriever](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/golden-retriever/)
4.   [German Shepherd Dog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-shepherd-dog/)
5.   Dachshund

The German Shorthaired Pointer and the Bulldog also switched places from 2024 to 2025. The Bulldog was No. 9 in 2024 and moved to No. 10 for 2025. The GSP did the opposite, rising from No. 10 in 2024 to No. 9 in 2025.

Rottweilers, Beagles, German Shepherd Dogs, Golden Retrievers, Labrador Retrievers, and French Bulldogs all stayed in the same ranking spot year over year.

## Big Shifts of Popularity for 2025

With 202 breeds in the rankings, 2025 saw some major shifts in breed popularity. Some breeds saw climbs of nearly 30 spots, while others fell in popularity by the same amount. It’s important to note that while some breeds move down in the rankings, it may not mean that they’ve become less popular — it may just mean that another breed has become more popular and moved up.

Some breeds also stayed in the exact same spot, which in most cases means the rankings shifted around it in a way that kept it in the same spot. For example, one breed may be at No. 30 year-over-year, but that could mean that one breed moved up in popularity while another moved down, cancelling out any obvious movement for certain breeds.

### Climbing the Rankings

Some breeds that gained momentum from 2024 to 2025 were working breeds and hunting breeds. The [Bergamasco Sheepdog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bergamasco-sheepdog/), though still towards the bottom of the rankings, went from No. 200 to No. 183, a 17-spot jump. The [English Foxhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/english-foxhound/) and the [Black and Tan Coonhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/black-and-tan-coonhound/) were both up 14 spots, from No. 201 to 187 and No. 151 to 137, respectively. The [English Toy Spaniel](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/english-toy-spaniel/), [Irish Setter](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/irish-setter/), and [Field Spaniel](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/field-spaniel/) all went up 12 spots in the rankings, and the [Greater Swiss Mountain Dog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/greater-swiss-mountain-dog/) and [Norwegian Buhund](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/norwegian-buhund/) were up 11. The [Pointer](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/pointer/) was up 10 spots from No. 121 to 111, and the [Treeing Walker Coonhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/treeing-walker-coonhound/), [Neapolitan Mastiff](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/neapolitan-mastiff/), and [Scottish Deerhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/scottish-deerhound/) were up nine spots from 2024.

# 2024 most popular dog breed is announced

Author(s)[_Abi Bautista-Alejandre, Assistant Editor_](https://www.dvm360.com/authors/abi-bautista-alejandre-assistant-editor)

The American Kennel Club has released the top 10 most popular dog breeds of 2024

Advertisement

![Image 3: Photo: belyaaa/Adobe Stock](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/0vv8moc6/dvm360/d47a28d32c5dd6d5454aaff1822205ff38485f5f-5472x3648.jpg/AdobeStock_268211828.jpeg?w=5472&max-h=3648&fit=crop&auto=format)

Photo: belyaaa/Adobe Stock

![Image 4](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/0vv8moc6/dvm360/d47a28d32c5dd6d5454aaff1822205ff38485f5f-5472x3648.jpg/AdobeStock_268211828.jpeg?fit=crop&auto=format)

According to registration statistics by the American Kennel Club (AKC)—a nonprofit organization maintaining a registry of purebred dogs—the French bulldog was the most popular dog breed in the United States in 2024. This marks the third consecutive year that the breed has claimed the top spot.

“The Frenchie has solidified itself as America’s sweetheart, and it’s no surprise why. They are fabulous companions for a variety of people,” Gina DiNardo, AKC executive secretary said in an organizational release.1

**2024's 10 most popular dog breeds in the US 1:**

1.   French Bulldog

1.   Labrador Retriever

1.   Golden Retriever

1.   German Shepherd Dog

1.   Poodle

1.   Dachshund

1.   Beagle

1.   Rottweiler

1.   Bulldog

1.   German Shorthaired Pointer

**Top 10 most popular breeds in 2023 1:**

1.   French Bulldog

1.   Labrador Retriever

1.   Golden Retriever

1.   German Shepherd Dog

1.   Poodle

1.   Dachshund

1.   Bulldog

1.   Beagle

1.   Rottweiler

1.   German Shorthaired Pointer

Although the French bulldog remains at the top of the list of dog registrations the US, Cane Corsos have seen an increase in registrations since the breed was recognized by the AKC in 2010, according to the organization. Over the past 10 years, the Cane Corso has advanced from 47th place in 2014 to 14th 2024—a 414% increase.

“...the Cane Corso is one to watch, as it has consistently increased in popularity since becoming recognized,” said DiNardo.1 “Corsi are majestic and intensely loyal, but not for everyone. As with any breed, we can’t stress enough the importance of doing your research to find the right breed for your lifestyle and to ensure that you’re getting a well-bred dog from a responsible breeder.”

Other breeds that have moved up or down the registrations list in 2024 include 1:

Advertisement

*   Staffordshire Bull Terrier: Went from #72 in 2023 to #63 in 2024
*   Chinese Crested: Went from #79 in 2023 to #68 in 2024
*   American Staffordshire Terrier: Went from #95 in 2023 to #77 in 2024
*   American Eskimo Dog: Went from #129 in 2023 to #116 in 2024
*   Bracco Italiano: Went from #152 in 2023 to #132 in 2024
*   German Pinscher: Went from #151 in 2023 to #133 in 2024

Breeds that have shown large increases in popularity over the last decade include the Boykin Spaniel, which rose from 108th place in 2014 to 65th in 2024; the Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever, moving from 99th to 69th place; and the Beauceron, which advanced from 145th to 100th place.1

### **About the French bulldog**

Recognized as a breed in 1898 by the AKC, the French bulldog has an average height of 11 to 13 inches and typically weighs under 28 lbs. Moreover, this breed has a life expectancy of 11 to 12 years.2

French bulldogs, according the AKC, are playful, smart, and adaptable animals that are affectionate with family. Moreover, these dogs do not bark often, typically only barking to alert owners, and do not require much outdoor exercise.

These dogs have a “front-heavy” structure that render them unable to swim.2 Due to their flat faces, French bulldogs are susceptible to breathing problems, making them ill-suited for hot or humid weather.2 Their flat faces also make them more sensitive to anesthesia.

Health conditions observed in this breed include cherry eye, entropion, skin allergies and autoimmune skin disorders.2 According to the AKC, the National Breed Club recommends French bulldogs obtain a patella, hip, and ophthalmologist evaluation, as well as a cardiac examination.2

# 2024 most popular dog breed is announced

Author(s)[_Abi Bautista-Alejandre, Assistant Editor_](https://www.dvm360.com/authors/abi-bautista-alejandre-assistant-editor)

The American Kennel Club has released the top 10 most popular dog breeds of 2024

Advertisement

![Image 3: Photo: belyaaa/Adobe Stock](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/0vv8moc6/dvm360/d47a28d32c5dd6d5454aaff1822205ff38485f5f-5472x3648.jpg/AdobeStock_268211828.jpeg?w=5472&max-h=3648&fit=crop&auto=format)

Photo: belyaaa/Adobe Stock

![Image 4](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/0vv8moc6/dvm360/d47a28d32c5dd6d5454aaff1822205ff38485f5f-5472x3648.jpg/AdobeStock_268211828.jpeg?fit=crop&auto=format)

According to registration statistics by the American Kennel Club (AKC)—a nonprofit organization maintaining a registry of purebred dogs—the French bulldog was the most popular dog breed in the United States in 2024. This marks the third consecutive year that the breed has claimed the top spot.

“The Frenchie has solidified itself as America’s sweetheart, and it’s no surprise why. They are fabulous companions for a variety of people,” Gina DiNardo, AKC executive secretary said in an organizational release.1

**2024's 10 most popular dog breeds in the US 1:**

1.   French Bulldog

1.   Labrador Retriever

1.   Golden Retriever

1.   German Shepherd Dog

1.   Poodle

1.   Dachshund

1.   Beagle

1.   Rottweiler

1.   Bulldog

1.   German Shorthaired Pointer

**Top 10 most popular breeds in 2023 1:**

1.   French Bulldog

1.   Labrador Retriever

1.   Golden Retriever

1.   German Shepherd Dog

1.   Poodle

1.   Dachshund

1.   Bulldog

1.   Beagle

1.   Rottweiler

1.   German Shorthaired Pointer

Although the French bulldog remains at the top of the list of dog registrations the US, Cane Corsos have seen an increase in registrations since the breed was recognized by the AKC in 2010, according to the organization. Over the past 10 years, the Cane Corso has advanced from 47th place in 2014 to 14th 2024—a 414% increase.

“...the Cane Corso is one to watch, as it has consistently increased in popularity since becoming recognized,” said DiNardo.1 “Corsi are majestic and intensely loyal, but not for everyone. As with any breed, we can’t stress enough the importance of doing your research to find the right breed for your lifestyle and to ensure that you’re getting a well-bred dog from a responsible breeder.”

Other breeds that have moved up or down the registrations list in 2024 include 1:

Advertisement

*   Staffordshire Bull Terrier: Went from #72 in 2023 to #63 in 2024
*   Chinese Crested: Went from #79 in 2023 to #68 in 2024
*   American Staffordshire Terrier: Went from #95 in 2023 to #77 in 2024
*   American Eskimo Dog: Went from #129 in 2023 to #116 in 2024
*   Bracco Italiano: Went from #152 in 2023 to #132 in 2024
*   German Pinscher: Went from #151 in 2023 to #133 in 2024

Breeds that have shown large increases in popularity over the last decade include the Boykin Spaniel, which rose from 108th place in 2014 to 65th in 2024; the Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever, moving from 99th to 69th place; and the Beauceron, which advanced from 145th to 100th place.1

### **About the French bulldog**

Recognized as a breed in 1898 by the AKC, the French bulldog has an average height of 11 to 13 inches and typically weighs under 28 lbs. Moreover, this breed has a life expectancy of 11 to 12 years.2

French bulldogs, according the AKC, are playful, smart, and adaptable animals that are affectionate with family. Moreover, these dogs do not bark often, typically only barking to alert owners, and do not require much outdoor exercise.

These dogs have a “front-heavy” structure that render them unable to swim.2 Due to their flat faces, French bulldogs are susceptible to breathing problems, making them ill-suited for hot or humid weather.2 Their flat faces also make them more sensitive to anesthesia.

Health conditions observed in this breed include cherry eye, entropion, skin allergies and autoimmune skin disorders.2 According to the AKC, the National Breed Club recommends French bulldogs obtain a patella, hip, and ophthalmologist evaluation, as well as a cardiac examination.2

# AKC reveals top 3 most popular dog breeds of 2024

![Image 3](https://i.abcnewsfe.com/a/cd94ea7e-a8fc-41b2-831f-25ebbd5f70d5/dog-1-abc-er-250318_1742315492319_hpMain_16x9.jpg?w=992)

Video 1[Video 2](blob:https://abcnews.com/8592a937-b036-4ef7-9e22-bd6c109c086c)

American Kennel Club reveals most popular dog breeds of 2025

ABC News

By[Yi-Jin Yu](https://abcnews.com/author/yi_jin_yu)

March 18, 2025, 5:06 PM

*     

The [French bulldog](https://www.goodmorningamerica.com/living/video/french-bulldog-pawfect-tic-tac-toe-98564486) is the American Kennel Club's top dog for the third straight year!

The AKC this week announced the top three dog breeds are French bulldogs, [Labrador retrievers](https://www.goodmorningamerica.com/living/video/watch-excited-labrador-tour-familys-1st-home-112902466) and [golden retrievers](https://www.goodmorningamerica.com/living/video/golden-retriever-toddler-share-adorable-cuddles-119797189).

French bulldogs, who were named top dog for 2022 and [in 2023,](https://www.goodmorningamerica.com/living/story/top-dog-meet-years-popular-dog-breeds-97875173) returned to the head of the pack [for the past year, 2024,](https://www.goodmorningamerica.com/living/story/american-kennel-club-popular-dog-breeds-108292781) as more people are choosing them for their small size, which makes them suitable for apartment living, according to the AKC.

[Related French bulldog revealed as most popular dog breed by American Kennel Club](https://www.goodmorningamerica.com/living/story/american-kennel-club-popular-dog-breeds-108292781)

[](https://www.goodmorningamerica.com/living/story/american-kennel-club-popular-dog-breeds-108292781)

![Image 4](https://i.abcnewsfe.com/a/cd94ea7e-a8fc-41b2-831f-25ebbd5f70d5/dog-1-abc-er-250318_1742315492319_hpMain_16x9.jpg)

American Kennel Club has named the Labrador retriever, the French bulldog and the golden retriever as the three most popular dog breeds of 2025.

ABC News

"I think, one, they're adorable … but also, I think as we do smaller living, and more people live in apartments, they're highly adaptable. They're good in small spaces," Brandi Hunter Munden, AKC's vice president of public relations and communications, told "Good Morning America."

"They're lovebugs. They just want to be with you most of the time and I think that's what really attracts people to them," Munden added.

![Image 5](https://i.abcnewsfe.com/a/84cfc363-8eb0-4441-b688-a3ff99185574/dogs-3-abc-er-250318_1742315656159_hpEmbed_16x9.jpg)

American Kennel Club has named the French bulldog as the third most popular dog breed of 2025.

ABC News

In addition to Frenchies, Munden said golden retrievers and Labrador retrievers are also well-liked for their personable traits.

"Goldens, we've all grown up with them. We see them all the time. They're highly adaptable. They're great with families," Munden continued. "They're going to go as much as you want to go, and that's really important to a lot of families, that they're great with kids and they're very gentle. They also do very well with service dogs."

![Image 6](https://i.abcnewsfe.com/a/5f53ee24-69c1-4ecc-ba4f-bdd714f14006/dogs-4-abc-er-250318_1742315656155_hpEmbed_16x9.jpg)

American Kennel Club has named the golden retriever as the third most popular dog breed of 2025.

ABC News

[Related This farm's golden retriever experience is a dog lover's dream destination](https://www.goodmorningamerica.com/travel/story/farms-golden-retriever-experience-dog-lovers-dream-destination-107919686)

[](https://www.goodmorningamerica.com/travel/story/farms-golden-retriever-experience-dog-lovers-dream-destination-107919686)

Like their counterparts in the retriever family, medium-size Labrador retrievers are also friendly and affectionate companions.

![Image 7](https://i.abcnewsfe.com/a/f743bc57-3e22-4fb2-81ad-59ae011e40dc/dogs-2-abc-er-250318_1742315656158_hpEmbed_16x9.jpg)

American Kennel Club has named the Labrador retriever as the third most popular dog breed of 2025.

ABC News

"As for labs, labs are energetic. Again, they're part of the fabric of who we are," said Munden. "They are a lot of fun, they love to hike, they love to run, and they also love to cuddle, which is probably No. 1 on most people's lists."

With any dog, Munden said potential owners should make sure to look up what they want in a furry friend first before they commit to raising and taking care of them.

# AKC reveals top 3 most popular dog breeds of 2024

![Image 3](https://i.abcnewsfe.com/a/cd94ea7e-a8fc-41b2-831f-25ebbd5f70d5/dog-1-abc-er-250318_1742315492319_hpMain_16x9.jpg?w=992)

Video 1[Video 2](blob:https://abcnews.com/8592a937-b036-4ef7-9e22-bd6c109c086c)

American Kennel Club reveals most popular dog breeds of 2025

ABC News

By[Yi-Jin Yu](https://abcnews.com/author/yi_jin_yu)

March 18, 2025, 5:06 PM

*     

The [French bulldog](https://www.goodmorningamerica.com/living/video/french-bulldog-pawfect-tic-tac-toe-98564486) is the American Kennel Club's top dog for the third straight year!

The AKC this week announced the top three dog breeds are French bulldogs, [Labrador retrievers](https://www.goodmorningamerica.com/living/video/watch-excited-labrador-tour-familys-1st-home-112902466) and [golden retrievers](https://www.goodmorningamerica.com/living/video/golden-retriever-toddler-share-adorable-cuddles-119797189).

French bulldogs, who were named top dog for 2022 and [in 2023,](https://www.goodmorningamerica.com/living/story/top-dog-meet-years-popular-dog-breeds-97875173) returned to the head of the pack [for the past year, 2024,](https://www.goodmorningamerica.com/living/story/american-kennel-club-popular-dog-breeds-108292781) as more people are choosing them for their small size, which makes them suitable for apartment living, according to the AKC.

[Related French bulldog revealed as most popular dog breed by American Kennel Club](https://www.goodmorningamerica.com/living/story/american-kennel-club-popular-dog-breeds-108292781)

[](https://www.goodmorningamerica.com/living/story/american-kennel-club-popular-dog-breeds-108292781)

![Image 4](https://i.abcnewsfe.com/a/cd94ea7e-a8fc-41b2-831f-25ebbd5f70d5/dog-1-abc-er-250318_1742315492319_hpMain_16x9.jpg)

American Kennel Club has named the Labrador retriever, the French bulldog and the golden retriever as the three most popular dog breeds of 2025.

ABC News

"I think, one, they're adorable … but also, I think as we do smaller living, and more people live in apartments, they're highly adaptable. They're good in small spaces," Brandi Hunter Munden, AKC's vice president of public relations and communications, told "Good Morning America."

"They're lovebugs. They just want to be with you most of the time and I think that's what really attracts people to them," Munden added.

![Image 5](https://i.abcnewsfe.com/a/84cfc363-8eb0-4441-b688-a3ff99185574/dogs-3-abc-er-250318_1742315656159_hpEmbed_16x9.jpg)

American Kennel Club has named the French bulldog as the third most popular dog breed of 2025.

ABC News

In addition to Frenchies, Munden said golden retrievers and Labrador retrievers are also well-liked for their personable traits.

"Goldens, we've all grown up with them. We see them all the time. They're highly adaptable. They're great with families," Munden continued. "They're going to go as much as you want to go, and that's really important to a lot of families, that they're great with kids and they're very gentle. They also do very well with service dogs."

![Image 6](https://i.abcnewsfe.com/a/5f53ee24-69c1-4ecc-ba4f-bdd714f14006/dogs-4-abc-er-250318_1742315656155_hpEmbed_16x9.jpg)

American Kennel Club has named the golden retriever as the third most popular dog breed of 2025.

ABC News

[Related This farm's golden retriever experience is a dog lover's dream destination](https://www.goodmorningamerica.com/travel/story/farms-golden-retriever-experience-dog-lovers-dream-destination-107919686)

[](https://www.goodmorningamerica.com/travel/story/farms-golden-retriever-experience-dog-lovers-dream-destination-107919686)

Like their counterparts in the retriever family, medium-size Labrador retrievers are also friendly and affectionate companions.

![Image 7](https://i.abcnewsfe.com/a/f743bc57-3e22-4fb2-81ad-59ae011e40dc/dogs-2-abc-er-250318_1742315656158_hpEmbed_16x9.jpg)

American Kennel Club has named the Labrador retriever as the third most popular dog breed of 2025.

ABC News

"As for labs, labs are energetic. Again, they're part of the fabric of who we are," said Munden. "They are a lot of fun, they love to hike, they love to run, and they also love to cuddle, which is probably No. 1 on most people's lists."

With any dog, Munden said potential owners should make sure to look up what they want in a furry friend first before they commit to raising and taking care of them.

## Change over time

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_most_popular_dog_breeds&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Change over time")]

Between 1915 and 1945, [American Kennel Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Kennel_Club "American Kennel Club") statistics were collected on a five-year basis instead of every year. These figures show that between 1905 and 1935, the [Siberian Husky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siberian_Husky "Siberian Husky") was consistently in either first or second place. [Malteses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maltese_dog "Maltese dog") were the most popular dog breed from 1936 all the way through to 1952, when the [Beagle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beagle "Beagle") became the number one dog until 1959. [Poodles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poodle "Poodle") would become the most popular breed for the longest time period, reigning from 1960 to 1982, when the American Maltese once again took over until 1990. The [Labrador Retriever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labrador_Retriever "Labrador Retriever") held the title from 1991 until 2023. Since then, the [French Bulldog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Bulldog "French Bulldog") has been the most popular dog breed in America.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most_popular_dog_breeds#cite_note-1)

This article lists the **most popular [dog breeds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dog_breed "Dog breed")** by registrations in the US.

_Note: registrations shown are not the same as annual registrations, or as living individuals._

## Change over time

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_most_popular_dog_breeds&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Change over time")]

Between 1915 and 1945, [American Kennel Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Kennel_Club "American Kennel Club") statistics were collected on a five-year basis instead of every year. These figures show that between 1905 and 1935, the [Siberian Husky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siberian_Husky "Siberian Husky") was consistently in either first or second place. [Malteses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maltese_dog "Maltese dog") were the most popular dog breed from 1936 all the way through to 1952, when the [Beagle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beagle "Beagle") became the number one dog until 1959. [Poodles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poodle "Poodle") would become the most popular breed for the longest time period, reigning from 1960 to 1982, when the American Maltese once again took over until 1990. The [Labrador Retriever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labrador_Retriever "Labrador Retriever") held the title from 1991 until 2023. Since then, the [French Bulldog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Bulldog "French Bulldog") has been the most popular dog breed in America.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most_popular_dog_breeds#cite_note-1)

# The Top 10 Most Popular Dog Breeds of 2025

![Image 1](blob:http://localhost/d85ba33652270dcb9c83f2dce174c2fc)![Image 2: Sarah Kloepple](https://pet-health-content-media.chewy.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/22022939/skthumbnail-150x150.jpeg?w=96&q=75)

By
Sarah Kloepple

. Reviewed by [Veronica Higgs, DVM](https://www.petmd.com/author/dr-veronica-higgs)

Updated Mar. 18, 2026

![Image 3](blob:http://localhost/c0e04639f976dc22cde9e0d37f26043e)![Image 4: white french bulldog lying on a person's lap](https://pet-health-content-media.chewy.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/03015629/most-popular-dog-breed-1024x683.jpg?w=2048&q=75)

Istock/gollykim

The American Kennel Club (AKC) recently released its annual list of the most popular dog breeds, and this year’s results are largely similar to the last.

The French Bulldog maintained the title of the most popular dog breed in the U.S. for the fourth year in a row. But there were some shifts. The Dachshund moved up in popularity, securing a spot in the top five dog breeds for the first time, and the Bulldog swapped places with the German Shorthaired Pointer.

What other dog breeds were deemed the most popular in the country? We’ve got a rundown of the results, and what you can expect from each if you’re looking to add one of these sought-after breeds to your home.

### Key Takeaways

*   The French Bulldog has been the most popular dog breed since 2022.
*   Before the Frenchie, the Labrador Retriever held the title of most popular dog for 31 years.
*   Dachshunds and German Shorthaired Pointers both rose in popularity in 2025. 
*   Many popular dogs make great family dogs thanks to their friendly temperaments. 

## 1. French Bulldog

![Image 5: brown french bulldog, the most popular dog breed, walking on a sandy beach](https://pet-health-content-media.chewy.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/03015644/french-bulldog-beach-scaled.jpg)

Photo by Adobe Stock/otsphoto

The[French Bulldog](https://www.petmd.com/dog/breeds/french-bulldog)has been climbing the ranks in popularity over the last 10 years, according to the AKC. They were first named the most popular dog breed in 2022 and still hold that title today.

It’s not hard to see why—Frenchies, as they’re often called, are easygoing, happy, compact dogs with a good-natured temperament and a bright personality.

They enjoy[short walks](https://www.petmd.com/dog/general-health/how-often-should-you-walk-your-dog), [playing fetch](https://be.chewy.com/how-to-teach-dog-to-fetch/), and games of tug-of-war. Their smaller size is ideal for any type of home, which has no doubt contributed to their popularity.

[French Bulldogs are prone to a handful of health issues](https://www.petmd.com/dog/general-health/french-bulldog-health-issues), though, including[brachycephalic airway syndrome](https://www.petmd.com/dog/conditions/respiratory/brachycephalic-airway-syndrome-dogs),[ear infections](https://www.petmd.com/dog/conditions/how-treat-and-prevent-dog-ear-infections), and back injuries.

Frenchies, like other breeds, should be fed a size and age-appropriate diet, and cleaning their ears regularly can help prevent frequent ear infections.

## 2. Labrador Retriever

![Image 9: chocolate labrador retriever, one of the most popular dog breeds, running in a park](https://pet-health-content-media.chewy.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/03015651/labrador-retriever-chocolate.jpg)

Photo by iStock/THEPALMER

[Labrador Retrievers](https://www.petmd.com/dog/breeds/labrador-retriever)are known for their affectionate nature toward everyone they meet—even strangers—and they do exceptionally well with children and other dogs. This breed loves the water and makes a great companion for families who spend a lot of time outdoors.

Labrador Retrievers love to play and are known to be highly energetic throughout most of their lives. They should be fed a high-quality diet appropriate for their age and size, and exercised regularly to maintain a healthy weight. Frequent games of fetch will keep your Lab active.

Labs are a[generally healthy breed](https://www.petmd.com/dog/general-health/healthiest-dog-breeds), but common health issues include [hip](https://www.petmd.com/dog/conditions/musculoskeletal/hip-dysplasia-dogs) and [elbow dysplasia](https://www.petmd.com/dog/conditions/musculoskeletal/elbow-dysplasia-in-dogs), ear infections, and [exercise-induced collapse](https://www.petmd.com/dog/conditions/genetic/exercise-induced-collapse-dogs).

## 3. Golden Retriever

![Image 11: golden retriever, one of the most popular dog breeds, running in a park with a tennis ball in his mouth](https://pet-health-content-media.chewy.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/03015656/popular-breed-golden-retriever.jpg)

Photo by iStock/cmannphoto

Another one of the most popular breeds is the[Golden Retriever](https://www.petmd.com/dog/breeds/golden-retriever). They’re considered an[intelligent](https://www.petmd.com/dog/general-health/smartest-dog-breeds), loyal, easy-to-train, and very affectionate breed. Like Labs, Golden Retrievers make [wonderful family dogs](https://www.petmd.com/dog/general-health/best-family-dogs) because they’re great with young children and other pups.

Goldens enjoy a wide variety of activities, including[running](https://www.petmd.com/dog/general-health/how-to-safely-go-running-with-your-dog), long walks, retrieving, and[swimming](https://www.petmd.com/dog/slideshows/breeds/top-swimming-dog-breeds). They also make excellent therapy dogs and guide dogs for people with impaired vision. Goldens thrive with regular activity and enrichment, and being fed a large breed-specific diet.

## 4. German Shepherd

![Image 15: german shepherd, a popular dog breed, lying on a kitchen floor, tilting his head at the camera](https://pet-health-content-media.chewy.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/03015702/popular-breed-german-shepherd.jpg)

Photo by iStock/ChristopherBernard

[German Shepherds](https://www.petmd.com/dog/breeds/german-shepherd)are large yet agile, muscular and highly intelligent dogs. They’re a breed known for their confidence, loyalty, and bravery.

These pups love having a job to do, and German Shepherds are commonly used as working dogs in the military and police for patrolling, bomb sniffing, and search and rescue.A German shepherd named Mercedes also [won the herding group](https://www.foxsports.com/watch/fmc-bujiyughporlno95) in the 2024 Westminster Dog Show.

Although they[have a long life expectancy](https://www.petmd.com/dog/care/how-long-do-dogs-live)for a large breed dog, they are prone to health issues such as[gastric dilation and volvulus](https://www.petmd.com/dog/conditions/digestive/gastric-dilatation-volvulus-gdv-syndrome)(which can be life-threatening), as well as[cancer](https://www.petmd.com/dog/conditions/cancer/dog-tumors), allergies, and heart disease. German Shepherds should be fed a large breed-appropriate diet, and puppies should be fed a large breed puppy food.

## 5. Dachshund

![Image 18: one brown and one black dachshund, one of the most popular dog breeds, walking on leashes](https://pet-health-content-media.chewy.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/03015719/popular-breed-dachshund.jpg)

[Dachshunds](https://www.petmd.com/dog/breeds/dachshund)are commonly called “Doxies,” or “wiener dogs,” and they’re known for their long silhouette, short and muscular legs, brave and energetic personality, and alert nature. They’re also known for being willful, headstrong, playful, and mischievous.

Although Doxies are down for anything their favorite humans are doing, these pups aren’t built for extensive running, jumping, or swimming—all these activities can make them susceptible to [injuring their long back](https://www.petmd.com/dog/conditions/neurological/c_dg_intervertebral_disc_disease). Offering a ramp or dog stairs in the house is great injury-prevention for long-backed Dachshunds.

A few health issues to keep an eye on include hip dysplasia,[idiopathic epilepsy](https://www.petmd.com/dog/conditions/neurological/epilepsy-dogs), and[Von Willebrand disease](https://www.petmd.com/dog/conditions/cardiovascular/c_dg_von_willebrand_disease).

## 7. Beagle

![Image 26: tricolor beagle, a popular dog breed, sitting in front of a mountain landscape](https://pet-health-content-media.chewy.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/03015727/popular-breed-beagle.jpg)

Photo by iStock/Tetiana Garkusha

[Beagles](https://www.petmd.com/dog/breeds/beagle)are famously led by their nose. This makes them a curious breed, but they’re also loving, affectionate, and active. Their sense of smell keeps their nose to the ground, and they love wagging their tails.

Beagles are also very smart, but they can be willful and have a short attention span when it comes to training. They respond best when you tap into their food-motivated nature! Using snuffle mats during mealtime will offer your Beagle some mental stimulation using their nose.

## 8. Rottweiler

![Image 30: close-up of a big brown and black rottweiler head, which is one of the most popular dog breeds](https://pet-health-content-media.chewy.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/03015736/popular-breed-rottweiler.jpg)

Photo by iStock/Peter D

[Rottweilers](https://www.petmd.com/dog/breeds/rottweiler)are loyal dogs that are eager to please their humans. They’re intelligent and respond well to [positive reinforcement training](https://www.petmd.com/dog/behavior/how-to-train-a-dog-with-positive-reinforcement), but if they grow bored, they can develop unwanted behaviors to entertain themselves.

Providing [mental stimulation](https://www.petmd.com/dog/general-health/ways-to-keep-dog-mentally-stimulated) is important for Rottweilers. They’re fans of running,[hiking](https://www.petmd.com/dog/wellness/evr_dg_hiking_with_your_dog),[dock diving](https://www.petmd.com/dog/training/everything-about-dock-diving-dogs), and tracking. Despite how active they are, the breed is prone to health problems including obesity. Feeding your Rottweiler the recommended serving sizes of a vet-recommended diet will reduce the risk of obesity.

## 9. German Shorthaired Pointer

![Image 33: two brown and white flecked german shorthaired pointers, a popular dog breed standing in a truck bed](https://pet-health-content-media.chewy.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/03015753/popular-breed-gsp.jpg)

Photo by iStock/jjMiller11

[German Shorthaired Pointers](https://www.petmd.com/dog/breeds/german-shorthaired-pointer)(GSP for short) are known for their speed, agility, and endurance. They’re often trained as[hunting dogs](https://www.petmd.com/dog/general-health/best-hunting-dogs)and will point and signal when they’re trailing a game scent by stopping and standing with their nose pointing in the direction of the scent.

Despite their need for adventure, they’re typically a low-maintenance breed. Running, fetching, or [agility games](https://www.petmd.com/dog/training/dog-agility-101) are great ways to spend time with them. But be on the lookout for health issues such as bloat, hip dysplasia, and elbow dysplasia.

## 10. English Bulldog

![Image 35: close-up of a brown and white english bulldog, a popular dog breed](https://pet-health-content-media.chewy.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/03015744/popular-breed-bulldog.jpg)

Photo by iStock/Kenneth Horn

Another identifiable breed—thanks to their wide stance, muscular low profile, and flat and wrinkled face with an underbite—[Bulldogs](https://www.petmd.com/dog/breeds/bulldog)(commonly called English Bulldogs) are a popular dog breed with a laid-back attitude.

Though they have a reputation for laziness, but the breed does enjoy (and benefit from!) daily moderate exercise. Exercise could include brisk walks and backyard games of tug-of-war, but keep all exercise out of the sun—thanks to their[smooshed-in face](https://www.petmd.com/dog/general-health/flat-faced-dogs), Bulldogs[can easily overheat](https://www.petmd.com/dog/conditions/systemic/heatstroke-dogs).

Bulldogs should be fed a breed, age, and size appropriate diet to maintain a healthy weight.

# The Top 10 Most Popular Dog Breeds of 2025

![Image 1](blob:http://localhost/d85ba33652270dcb9c83f2dce174c2fc)![Image 2: Sarah Kloepple](https://pet-health-content-media.chewy.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/22022939/skthumbnail-150x150.jpeg?w=96&q=75)

Sarah Kloepple

. Reviewed by [Veronica Higgs, DVM](https://www.petmd.com/author/dr-veronica-higgs)

Updated Mar. 18, 2026

![Image 3](blob:http://localhost/c0e04639f976dc22cde9e0d37f26043e)![Image 4: white french bulldog lying on a person's lap](https://pet-health-content-media.chewy.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/03015629/most-popular-dog-breed-1024x683.jpg?w=2048&q=75)

Istock/gollykim

The American Kennel Club (AKC) recently released its annual list of the most popular dog breeds, and this year’s results are largely similar to the last.

The French Bulldog maintained the title of the most popular dog breed in the U.S. for the fourth year in a row. But there were some shifts. The Dachshund moved up in popularity, securing a spot in the top five dog breeds for the first time, and the Bulldog swapped places with the German Shorthaired Pointer.

What other dog breeds were deemed the most popular in the country? We’ve got a rundown of the results, and what you can expect from each if you’re looking to add one of these sought-after breeds to your home.

### Key Takeaways

*   The French Bulldog has been the most popular dog breed since 2022.
*   Before the Frenchie, the Labrador Retriever held the title of most popular dog for 31 years.
*   Dachshunds and German Shorthaired Pointers both rose in popularity in 2025. 
*   Many popular dogs make great family dogs thanks to their friendly temperaments. 

## 1. French Bulldog

![Image 5: brown french bulldog, the most popular dog breed, walking on a sandy beach](https://pet-health-content-media.chewy.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/03015644/french-bulldog-beach-scaled.jpg)

Photo by Adobe Stock/otsphoto

The[French Bulldog](https://www.petmd.com/dog/breeds/french-bulldog)has been climbing the ranks in popularity over the last 10 years, according to the AKC. They were first named the most popular dog breed in 2022 and still hold that title today.

It’s not hard to see why—Frenchies, as they’re often called, are easygoing, happy, compact dogs with a good-natured temperament and a bright personality.

They enjoy[short walks](https://www.petmd.com/dog/general-health/how-often-should-you-walk-your-dog), [playing fetch](https://be.chewy.com/how-to-teach-dog-to-fetch/), and games of tug-of-war. Their smaller size is ideal for any type of home, which has no doubt contributed to their popularity.

[French Bulldogs are prone to a handful of health issues](https://www.petmd.com/dog/general-health/french-bulldog-health-issues), though, including[brachycephalic airway syndrome](https://www.petmd.com/dog/conditions/respiratory/brachycephalic-airway-syndrome-dogs),[ear infections](https://www.petmd.com/dog/conditions/how-treat-and-prevent-dog-ear-infections), and back injuries.

Frenchies, like other breeds, should be fed a size and age-appropriate diet, and cleaning their ears regularly can help prevent frequent ear infections.

## 2. Labrador Retriever

![Image 9: chocolate labrador retriever, one of the most popular dog breeds, running in a park](https://pet-health-content-media.chewy.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/03015651/labrador-retriever-chocolate.jpg)

Photo by iStock/THEPALMER

[Labrador Retrievers](https://www.petmd.com/dog/breeds/labrador-retriever)are known for their affectionate nature toward everyone they meet—even strangers—and they do exceptionally well with children and other dogs. This breed loves the water and makes a great companion for families who spend a lot of time outdoors.

Labrador Retrievers love to play and are known to be highly energetic throughout most of their lives. They should be fed a high-quality diet appropriate for their age and size, and exercised regularly to maintain a healthy weight. Frequent games of fetch will keep your Lab active.

## 3. Golden Retriever

![Image 11: golden retriever, one of the most popular dog breeds, running in a park with a tennis ball in his mouth](https://pet-health-content-media.chewy.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/03015656/popular-breed-golden-retriever.jpg)

Photo by iStock/cmannphoto

Another one of the most popular breeds is the[Golden Retriever](https://www.petmd.com/dog/breeds/golden-retriever). They’re considered an[intelligent](https://www.petmd.com/dog/general-health/smartest-dog-breeds), loyal, easy-to-train, and very affectionate breed. Like Labs, Golden Retrievers make [wonderful family dogs](https://www.petmd.com/dog/general-health/best-family-dogs) because they’re great with young children and other pups.

Goldens enjoy a wide variety of activities, including[running](https://www.petmd.com/dog/general-health/how-to-safely-go-running-with-your-dog), long walks, retrieving, and[swimming](https://www.petmd.com/dog/slideshows/breeds/top-swimming-dog-breeds). They also make excellent therapy dogs and guide dogs for people with impaired vision. Goldens thrive with regular activity and enrichment, and being fed a large breed-specific diet.

## 4. German Shepherd

![Image 15: german shepherd, a popular dog breed, lying on a kitchen floor, tilting his head at the camera](https://pet-health-content-media.chewy.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/03015702/popular-breed-german-shepherd.jpg)

Photo by iStock/ChristopherBernard

[German Shepherds](https://www.petmd.com/dog/breeds/german-shepherd)are large yet agile, muscular and highly intelligent dogs. They’re a breed known for their confidence, loyalty, and bravery.

These pups love having a job to do, and German Shepherds are commonly used as working dogs in the military and police for patrolling, bomb sniffing, and search and rescue.A German shepherd named Mercedes also [won the herding group](https://www.foxsports.com/watch/fmc-bujiyughporlno95) in the 2024 Westminster Dog Show.

Although they[have a long life expectancy](https://www.petmd.com/dog/care/how-long-do-dogs-live)for a large breed dog, they are prone to health issues such as[gastric dilation and volvulus](https://www.petmd.com/dog/conditions/digestive/gastric-dilatation-volvulus-gdv-syndrome)(which can be life-threatening), as well as[cancer](https://www.petmd.com/dog/conditions/cancer/dog-tumors), allergies, and heart disease. German Shepherds should be fed a large breed-appropriate diet, and puppies should be fed a large breed puppy food.

## 5. Dachshund

![Image 18: one brown and one black dachshund, one of the most popular dog breeds, walking on leashes](https://pet-health-content-media.chewy.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/03015719/popular-breed-dachshund.jpg)

Photo by iStock/Timbicus

[Dachshunds](https://www.petmd.com/dog/breeds/dachshund)are commonly called “Doxies,” or “wiener dogs,” and they’re known for their long silhouette, short and muscular legs, brave and energetic personality, and alert nature. They’re also known for being willful, headstrong, playful, and mischievous.

Although Doxies are down for anything their favorite humans are doing, these pups aren’t built for extensive running, jumping, or swimming—all these activities can make them susceptible to [injuring their long back](https://www.petmd.com/dog/conditions/neurological/c_dg_intervertebral_disc_disease). Offering a ramp or dog stairs in the house is great injury-prevention for long-backed Dachshunds.

## 6. Poodle

As an athletic, smart, and good-natured breed, the Poodle rounds out the top five most popular dog breeds. This breed comes in [three distinct sizes](https://www.petmd.com/dog/general-health/types-of-poodles): [Standard](https://www.petmd.com/dog/breeds/c_dg_poodle), [Miniature](https://www.petmd.com/dog/breeds/miniature-poodle), and [Toy](https://www.petmd.com/dog/breeds/toy-poodle).

Their recognizable curly coat gives them their reputation as[“hypoallergenic” dogs](https://www.petmd.com/dog/general-health/hypoallergenic-dogs)and requires regular and consistent grooming by a professional to stay healthy and mat-free. Regular brushing and combing at home can help decrease tangles between grooming appointments.

## 8. Rottweiler

Every year the [American Kennel Club](http://akc.org/) releases our ranking of the most popular dog breeds based on AKC registration statistics for the previous year.

The [French Bulldog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/french-bulldog/) continues to top the rankings at the No. 1 spot for the fourth year in a row. The [Labrador Retriever](https://www.akc.org/press-releases/labrador-retriever-celebrates-30-years-top-spot-french-bulldog-overtakes-german-shepherd-dog-number-2-spot/), who had a 31-year run as the most popular breed, is in the No. 2 spot for the third year in a row. In 2025, the Poodle moved out of the top five, replaced by the [Dachshund](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/dachshund/). Many other breeds have moved spots from 2024 to 2025. Below, find ranked annual lists of [AKC-recognized breeds](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/).

    5.   Dachshund

Every year the [American Kennel Club](http://akc.org/) releases our ranking of the most popular dog breeds based on AKC registration statistics for the previous year.

The [French Bulldog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/french-bulldog/) continues to top the rankings at the No. 1 spot for the fourth year in a row. The [Labrador Retriever](https://www.akc.org/press-releases/labrador-retriever-celebrates-30-years-top-spot-french-bulldog-overtakes-german-shepherd-dog-number-2-spot/), who had a 31-year run as the most popular breed, is in the No. 2 spot for the third year in a row. In 2025, the Poodle moved out of the top five, replaced by the [Dachshund](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/dachshund/). Many other breeds have moved spots from 2024 to 2025. Below, find ranked annual lists of [AKC-recognized breeds](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/).

*   **2025**+

    1.   French Bulldog
    2.   Labrador Retriever
    3.   [Golden Retriever](http://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/golden-retriever)
    4.   [German Shepherd Dog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-shepherd-dog/)
    5.   Dachshund

Full 2025 most popular dog breed list

*   **2024**+

    1.   French Bulldog
    2.   Labrador Retriever
    3.   Golden Retriever
    4.   German Shepherd Dog
    5.   [Poodle](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/poodle-standard/)

Full 2024 most popular dog breed list

*   **2023**+

    1.   French Bulldog
    2.   Labrador Retriever

French bulldogs have surged in popularity over the past decade, driven in part by their small size and adaptability to urban living, making them a common choice for city and apartment dwellers.

The breed ranked No. 14 in 2012 before climbing to No. 2 by 2021. It overtook the Labrador retriever in 2022 to become the nation’s most popular breed, a position it has maintained for four consecutive years.

*   **Stable rankings:** Breeds like the Boston Terrier, Havanese and Basset Hound held steady year over year.

#### The Brief

*       *   The French bulldog ranked No. 1 for a fourth straight year in 2025.
    *   Labrador retrievers remained among the most popular breeds.
    *   The top 10 saw minor shifts, including the dachshund entering the top five.

The French bulldog has once again claimed the top spot as America’s most popular dog breed, marking its fourth consecutive year leading the American Kennel Club’s annual rankings.

Undo

The French bulldog held onto its title as the nation’s most popular dog breed for a fourth consecutive year in 2025, after first ending the Labrador retriever’s 31-year run at No. 1 in 2022. Labrador retrievers, however, remain among the most popular breeds in the U.S.

Dig deeper:

The American Kennel Club has recognized 205 breeds since its founding in 1884, with 202 included in the 2025 registration statistics. Three additional breeds were recognized in 2026 and will be reflected in next year’s rankings, while others continue to advance toward recognition through the AKC Foundation Stock Service and Miscellaneous Class.

## The French bulldog

Big picture view:

French bulldogs have surged in popularity over the past decade, driven in part by their small size and adaptability to urban living, making them a common choice for city and apartment dwellers.

The breed ranked No. 14 in 2012 before climbing to No. 2 by 2021. It overtook the Labrador retriever in 2022 to become the nation’s most popular breed, a position it has maintained for four consecutive years.

## Other key takeaways

*   **Wide movement in rankings:** Among 202 breeds, some jumped nearly 30 spots while others fell by similar margins; declines don’t necessarily mean decreased popularity.
*   **Biggest climbers:** Wirehaired Vizsla (+29) led gains; several working and hunting breeds also rose, including Bergamasco Sheepdog (+17) and English Foxhound (+14).
*   **Notable risers:** Cane Corso neared the top 10 (No. 11), while Border Collies and Pomeranians saw smaller gains.
*   **Biggest drops:** Greyhound (-33), Briard and Black Russian Terrier (-27 each), and Kerry Blue Terrier (-20) saw the steepest declines.
*   **Stable rankings:** Breeds like the Boston Terrier, Havanese and Basset Hound held steady year over year.
*   **New additions:** The Danish-Swedish Farmdog debuted at No. 170 in 2025; three newly recognized breeds will join the rankings in 2026.
