The American Kennel Club has unveiled its list of the five most popular dog breeds across the country.

On Wednesday, March 18, Brandi Munden, vice president of communications and public relations at the American Kennel Club, stopped by TODAY to exclusively reveal the five breeds.

A furry friend from each breed then joined the show to strut their stuff and show off some of their best attributes, from their shiny coats to their outgoing personalities.

Without further ado, here are the top breeds based on the AKC’s 2025 annual registration numbers.

## 5. Dachshund

![Image 20: The Dachshund has captured the hearts of many people in the U.S.](https://media-cldnry.s-nbcnews.com/image/upload/t_fit-760w,f_avif,q_auto:best/rockcms/2026-03/dachshund-lc-260317-363172.jpg)

The dachshund has captured the hearts of many people in the U.S.Getty Images / Getty Images/iStockphoto

The dachshunds, represented on TODAY by the intelligent Pretzel, cracked the top five after just missing the cutoff last year. The dogs, which were initially bred to be independent hunters of badgers, are small but mighty and great problem solvers.

Dachshunds come in two sizes (standard and miniature) and three coat types (smooth, wirehaired and longhaired).

## 4. German Shepherd Dog

![Image 21: A German shepherd dog is among the top five most popular dog breeds in the country.](https://media-cldnry.s-nbcnews.com/image/upload/t_fit-760w,f_avif,q_auto:best/rockcms/2026-03/german-shepherd-dog-lc-260317-788ab9.jpg)

A German shepherd dog is among the top five most popular dog breeds in the country.Getty Images

The German shepherd, represented by Eamonn on TODAY, has held onto its fourth place spot. The versatile breed can help perform police work and search and rescue missions in addition to acting as a friendly companion or a service dog.

## 3. Golden Retriever

![Image 22: The Golden Retriever continues to be a popular breed in the US, according to the AKC.](https://media-cldnry.s-nbcnews.com/image/upload/t_fit-760w,f_avif,q_auto:best/rockcms/2026-03/golden-retriever-lc-260317-2edc54.jpg)

The golden retriever continues to be a popular breed in the US, according to the AKC.Getty Images

Also maintaining its spot on the list, in third place is the golden retriever, represented by Griswold. Golden retrievers are known for being great with children and easy to train due to their energetic personalities and their strong bond with their owners.

## 2. Labrador Retriever

![Image 23: Labrador Retrievers were the second most popular dog breeds in the country last year, according to the American Kennel Club.](https://media-cldnry.s-nbcnews.com/image/upload/t_fit-760w,f_avif,q_auto:best/rockcms/2026-03/labrador-retrievers-lc-260317-7576d5.jpg)

Labrador retrievers were the second most popular dog breeds in the country last year, according to the American Kennel Club.Getty Images

The Labrador retriever has, again, placed second on the list. Represented by Hola on TODAY, the breed is known for being family friendly and outgoing with an even temperament. They love to be included in family activities, are eagerness to please and enjoy having room to play.

## 1. French Bulldog

![Image 24: The French Bulldog is the American Kennel Club most popular dog breed in the country.](https://media-cldnry.s-nbcnews.com/image/upload/t_fit-760w,f_avif,q_auto:best/rockcms/2026-03/French-Bulldog-lc-260317-27bb93.jpg)

The French bulldog is the American Kennel Club most popular dog breed in the country.Getty Images 

Taking the crown for the fourth year in a row is the French bulldog, represented by Auggie. While the breed is affectionate and playful, French bulldogs are also protective, which makes them the perfect watchdogs. French bulldogs are great companions for all ages.

Each year, the AKC compiles its list using its annual registration numbers of the breeds it recognizes. For 2025, the dachshund replaced the poodle, which was previously in the top five. Rounding out the top 10 for 2024 were the beagle, Rottweiler, bulldog and German shorthaired pointer.

The American Kennel Club has unveiled its list of the five most popular dog breeds across the country.

On Wednesday, March 18, Brandi Munden, vice president of communications and public relations at the American Kennel Club, stopped by TODAY to exclusively reveal the five breeds.

A furry friend from each breed then joined the show to strut their stuff and show off some of their best attributes, from their shiny coats to their outgoing personalities.

Without further ado, here are the top breeds based on the AKC’s 2025 annual registration numbers.

## 5. Dachshund

![Image 20: The Dachshund has captured the hearts of many people in the U.S.](https://media-cldnry.s-nbcnews.com/image/upload/t_fit-760w,f_avif,q_auto:best/rockcms/2026-03/dachshund-lc-260317-363172.jpg)

The dachshund has captured the hearts of many people in the U.S.Getty Images / Getty Images/iStockphoto

The dachshunds, represented on TODAY by the intelligent Pretzel, cracked the top five after just missing the cutoff last year. The dogs, which were initially bred to be independent hunters of badgers, are small but mighty and great problem solvers.

Dachshunds come in two sizes (standard and miniature) and three coat types (smooth, wirehaired and longhaired).

## 4. German Shepherd Dog

![Image 21: A German shepherd dog is among the top five most popular dog breeds in the country.](https://media-cldnry.s-nbcnews.com/image/upload/t_fit-760w,f_avif,q_auto:best/rockcms/2026-03/german-shepherd-dog-lc-260317-788ab9.jpg)

A German shepherd dog is among the top five most popular dog breeds in the country.Getty Images

The German shepherd, represented by Eamonn on TODAY, has held onto its fourth place spot. The versatile breed can help perform police work and search and rescue missions in addition to acting as a friendly companion or a service dog.

## 3. Golden Retriever

![Image 22: The Golden Retriever continues to be a popular breed in the US, according to the AKC.](https://media-cldnry.s-nbcnews.com/image/upload/t_fit-760w,f_avif,q_auto:best/rockcms/2026-03/golden-retriever-lc-260317-2edc54.jpg)

The golden retriever continues to be a popular breed in the US, according to the AKC.Getty Images

Also maintaining its spot on the list, in third place is the golden retriever, represented by Griswold. Golden retrievers are known for being great with children and easy to train due to their energetic personalities and their strong bond with their owners.

## 2. Labrador Retriever

![Image 23: Labrador Retrievers were the second most popular dog breeds in the country last year, according to the American Kennel Club.](https://media-cldnry.s-nbcnews.com/image/upload/t_fit-760w,f_avif,q_auto:best/rockcms/2026-03/labrador-retrievers-lc-260317-7576d5.jpg)

Labrador retrievers were the second most popular dog breeds in the country last year, according to the American Kennel Club.Getty Images

The Labrador retriever has, again, placed second on the list. Represented by Hola on TODAY, the breed is known for being family friendly and outgoing with an even temperament. They love to be included in family activities, are eagerness to please and enjoy having room to play.

## 1. French Bulldog

![Image 24: The French Bulldog is the American Kennel Club most popular dog breed in the country.](https://media-cldnry.s-nbcnews.com/image/upload/t_fit-760w,f_avif,q_auto:best/rockcms/2026-03/French-Bulldog-lc-260317-27bb93.jpg)

The French bulldog is the American Kennel Club most popular dog breed in the country.Getty Images 

Taking the crown for the fourth year in a row is the French bulldog, represented by Auggie. While the breed is affectionate and playful, French bulldogs are also protective, which makes them the perfect watchdogs. French bulldogs are great companions for all ages.

Each year, the AKC compiles its list using its annual registration numbers of the breeds it recognizes. For 2025, the dachshund replaced the poodle, which was previously in the top five. Rounding out the top 10 for 2024 were the beagle, Rottweiler, bulldog and German shorthaired pointer.

# Most and Least Popular Dog Breeds, According to the AKC

  

March 20, 2025[Featured](https://stevedalepetworld.com/blog/category/featured/) • [dog breeding](https://stevedalepetworld.com/blog/category/dog-breeding/) • [dogs](https://stevedalepetworld.com/blog/category/dogs/)

![Image 2](https://stevedalepetworld.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/french-bulldog.jpeg)

### Share

[](https://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fstevedalepetworld.com%2Fblog%2Fmost-and-least-popular-dog-breeds-according-to-the-akc%2F)

[](https://twitter.com/share?url=https%3A%2F%2Fstevedalepetworld.com%2Fblog%2Fmost-and-least-popular-dog-breeds-according-to-the-akc%2F)

[](mailto:?body=https%3A%2F%2Fstevedalepetworld.com%2Fblog%2Fmost-and-least-popular-dog-breeds-according-to-the-akc%2F)

For the second consecutive year, the French Bulldog remains the most common dog breed, at least according to the American Kennel Club (AKC).

Before reading too much into this list, while the AKC may be the largest registry of pure-bred dogs in the U.S., most U.S. dogs are not pure-bred dogs and many who have one or more pure-bred dogs never register. Still, the AKc list of most popular dog breeds is thought-provoking or interesting at some level, and may demonstrate trends.

Last year, the Frenchie took over the number one position from the Labrador Retriever, who was previously entrenched for 31 years as America’s top dog.

So, why Frenchies? They’re fun, that’s for sure. They’re also a perfect size for apartment dogs.

What’s more lots of celebs have French Bulldogs, which has increased both interest in the breed (and the cost of purchasing), including Lady Gaga, Reese Witherspoon, Hugh Jackman, Chrissy Teigen and John Legend, and many others.

And those schmoosed in faces may be cute but they are also brachycephalic dogs, and commonly can have great difficulty breathing, and especially in the U.S. suffer from Brachycephalic Obstructive Airway Syndrome (BOAS). They can have difficulty getting air into their lungs and can’t easily breathe through their nose and have an elongated soft palate obstructing their larynx or windpipe. This lifetime of turbulence may also cause the larynx to thicken. As a result, they also may have narrowing of the windpipe or trachea. BOAS impacts quality of life often daily as well as shortening lifespan. This is so much an issue at the[World Small Animal Veterinary Association recently pronounced extreme brachycephalic dogs an “international canine welfare crisis.”](https://stevedalepetworld.com/blog/world-small-animal-veterinary-association-taking-a-stand-against-extreme-brachycephalic-breeding/)

While individual responsible breeders and the French Bulldog Club have for years taken action to deal with this issue; the AKC appear to have no proactive position. What’s more, many of Frenchies are sold at pet stores and are therefore likely are likely from puppy mills where responsible breeding doesn’t exist. The AKC has no problem with that either.

#### **Climbing the Pop Charts**

Unsure why by the Kerry Blue Terrier – hailing from Ireland – moved up a whopping 25 places from number 160 to 135 on the AKC list. Perhaps, that’s because the breed is presumed hypoallergenic, at least some people with allergies can do well.

Another winner is the Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever – moving up from number 83 to 69 on the AKC chart. The Duck Tolling Retriever is a bred which is just slightly smaller than the ever popular Golden Retriever.

The American Staffordshire Terrier, long considered a great family dog, for those in the know – moved up from number 95 in popularity to 77. Also, making a big push was the Boykin Spanei which went from number 75 to the 65 th most popular. Still, do most people even know what this breed is?

#### Fall from Grace

Such sad news for the regal Saluka, dropping on the AKC chart from number 120 to number 141. The Shar-Pei, the breed which Chinese zoos have reportedly used to impersonate a giant panda – despite all the press – fell from number 70 to number 83. The rollickin’ Old English Sheepdog also had a bad year, dipping 12 places from number 77 to number 89,

Two large breeds dropped as well, the Neopolitan Mastiff and Great Pyrenees, the former from 118 to currently ranking 128, and the latter dropping to 74 from last year’s number 64.

# Most and Least Popular Dog Breeds, According to the AKC

  

March 20, 2025[Featured](https://stevedalepetworld.com/blog/category/featured/) • [dog breeding](https://stevedalepetworld.com/blog/category/dog-breeding/) • [dogs](https://stevedalepetworld.com/blog/category/dogs/)

![Image 2](https://stevedalepetworld.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/french-bulldog.jpeg)

### Share

[](https://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fstevedalepetworld.com%2Fblog%2Fmost-and-least-popular-dog-breeds-according-to-the-akc%2F)

[](https://twitter.com/share?url=https%3A%2F%2Fstevedalepetworld.com%2Fblog%2Fmost-and-least-popular-dog-breeds-according-to-the-akc%2F)

[](mailto:?body=https%3A%2F%2Fstevedalepetworld.com%2Fblog%2Fmost-and-least-popular-dog-breeds-according-to-the-akc%2F)

For the second consecutive year, the French Bulldog remains the most common dog breed, at least according to the American Kennel Club (AKC).

Before reading too much into this list, while the AKC may be the largest registry of pure-bred dogs in the U.S., most U.S. dogs are not pure-bred dogs and many who have one or more pure-bred dogs never register. Still, the AKc list of most popular dog breeds is thought-provoking or interesting at some level, and may demonstrate trends.

Last year, the Frenchie took over the number one position from the Labrador Retriever, who was previously entrenched for 31 years as America’s top dog.

So, why Frenchies? They’re fun, that’s for sure. They’re also a perfect size for apartment dogs.

What’s more lots of celebs have French Bulldogs, which has increased both interest in the breed (and the cost of purchasing), including Lady Gaga, Reese Witherspoon, Hugh Jackman, Chrissy Teigen and John Legend, and many others.

And those schmoosed in faces may be cute but they are also brachycephalic dogs, and commonly can have great difficulty breathing, and especially in the U.S. suffer from Brachycephalic Obstructive Airway Syndrome (BOAS). They can have difficulty getting air into their lungs and can’t easily breathe through their nose and have an elongated soft palate obstructing their larynx or windpipe. This lifetime of turbulence may also cause the larynx to thicken. As a result, they also may have narrowing of the windpipe or trachea. BOAS impacts quality of life often daily as well as shortening lifespan. This is so much an issue at the[World Small Animal Veterinary Association recently pronounced extreme brachycephalic dogs an “international canine welfare crisis.”](https://stevedalepetworld.com/blog/world-small-animal-veterinary-association-taking-a-stand-against-extreme-brachycephalic-breeding/)

While individual responsible breeders and the French Bulldog Club have for years taken action to deal with this issue; the AKC appear to have no proactive position. What’s more, many of Frenchies are sold at pet stores and are therefore likely are likely from puppy mills where responsible breeding doesn’t exist. The AKC has no problem with that either.

#### **Climbing the Pop Charts**

Unsure why by the Kerry Blue Terrier – hailing from Ireland – moved up a whopping 25 places from number 160 to 135 on the AKC list. Perhaps, that’s because the breed is presumed hypoallergenic, at least some people with allergies can do well.

Another winner is the Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever – moving up from number 83 to 69 on the AKC chart. The Duck Tolling Retriever is a bred which is just slightly smaller than the ever popular Golden Retriever.

The American Staffordshire Terrier, long considered a great family dog, for those in the know – moved up from number 95 in popularity to 77. Also, making a big push was the Boykin Spanei which went from number 75 to the 65 th most popular. Still, do most people even know what this breed is?

#### Fall from Grace

Such sad news for the regal Saluka, dropping on the AKC chart from number 120 to number 141. The Shar-Pei, the breed which Chinese zoos have reportedly used to impersonate a giant panda – despite all the press – fell from number 70 to number 83. The rollickin’ Old English Sheepdog also had a bad year, dipping 12 places from number 77 to number 89,

Two large breeds dropped as well, the Neopolitan Mastiff and Great Pyrenees, the former from 118 to currently ranking 128, and the latter dropping to 74 from last year’s number 64.

This article lists the **most popular [dog breeds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dog_breed "Dog breed")** by registrations in the US.

_Note: registrations shown are not the same as annual registrations, or as living individuals._

## Change over time

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_most_popular_dog_breeds&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Change over time")]

Between 1915 and 1945, [American Kennel Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Kennel_Club "American Kennel Club") statistics were collected on a five-year basis instead of every year. These figures show that between 1905 and 1935, the [Siberian Husky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siberian_Husky "Siberian Husky") was consistently in either first or second place. [Malteses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maltese_dog "Maltese dog") were the most popular dog breed from 1936 all the way through to 1952, when the [Beagle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beagle "Beagle") became the number one dog until 1959. [Poodles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poodle "Poodle") would become the most popular breed for the longest time period, reigning from 1960 to 1982, when the American Maltese once again took over until 1990. The [Labrador Retriever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labrador_Retriever "Labrador Retriever") held the title from 1991 until 2023. Since then, the [French Bulldog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Bulldog "French Bulldog") has been the most popular dog breed in America.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most_popular_dog_breeds#cite_note-1)

This article lists the **most popular [dog breeds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dog_breed "Dog breed")** by registrations in the US.

_Note: registrations shown are not the same as annual registrations, or as living individuals._

## Change over time

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_most_popular_dog_breeds&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Change over time")]

Between 1915 and 1945, [American Kennel Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Kennel_Club "American Kennel Club") statistics were collected on a five-year basis instead of every year. These figures show that between 1905 and 1935, the [Siberian Husky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siberian_Husky "Siberian Husky") was consistently in either first or second place. [Malteses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maltese_dog "Maltese dog") were the most popular dog breed from 1936 all the way through to 1952, when the [Beagle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beagle "Beagle") became the number one dog until 1959. [Poodles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poodle "Poodle") would become the most popular breed for the longest time period, reigning from 1960 to 1982, when the American Maltese once again took over until 1990. The [Labrador Retriever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labrador_Retriever "Labrador Retriever") held the title from 1991 until 2023. Since then, the [French Bulldog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Bulldog "French Bulldog") has been the most popular dog breed in America.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most_popular_dog_breeds#cite_note-1)

The top 10 stayed relatively the same as previous years, but other breeds are gaining popularity. The [Finnish Lapphund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finnish_Lapphund "Finnish Lapphund") rose 32 spots to number 135. The lowest of the nationally recognized ranked dog breed was the [Sloughi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sloughi "Sloughi").

Every year the [American Kennel Club](http://akc.org/) releases our ranking of the most popular dog breeds based on AKC registration statistics for the previous year.

The [French Bulldog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/french-bulldog/) continues to top the rankings at the No. 1 spot for the fourth year in a row. The [Labrador Retriever](https://www.akc.org/press-releases/labrador-retriever-celebrates-30-years-top-spot-french-bulldog-overtakes-german-shepherd-dog-number-2-spot/), who had a 31-year run as the most popular breed, is in the No. 2 spot for the third year in a row. In 2025, the Poodle moved out of the top five, replaced by the [Dachshund](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/dachshund/). Many other breeds have moved spots from 2024 to 2025. Every year the [American Kennel Club](http://akc.org/) releases our ranking of the most popular dog breeds based on AKC registration statistics for the previous year.

The [French Bulldog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/french-bulldog/) continues to top the rankings at the No. 1 spot for the fourth year in a row. The [Labrador Retriever](https://www.akc.org/press-releases/labrador-retriever-celebrates-30-years-top-spot-french-bulldog-overtakes-german-shepherd-dog-number-2-spot/), who had a 31-year run as the most popular breed, is in the No. 2 spot for the third year in a row. In 2025, the Poodle moved out of the top five, replaced by the [Dachshund](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/dachshund/). Many other breeds have moved spots from 2024 to 2025. Below, find ranked annual lists of [AKC-recognized breeds](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/).

The American Kennel Club, the world’s largest registry of purebred dogs, uses registration statistics to rank the most popular breeds of the past year. The results for 2025 are in — the [French Bulldog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/french-bulldog/) takes the No. 1 spot once again!

2025 marks the fourth year in a row that the French Bulldog has been able to remain in the top spot. In 2022, they overthrew the [Labrador Retriever](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/labrador-retriever/)‘s [31-year reign](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/most-popular-dog-breeds-of-2021/) in the number one spot, where they’d been since the 1990s. But don’t worry — Labs are still amongst the most popular breeds in the United States.

The American Kennel Club has recognized 205 breeds since it was first founded in 1884, 202 of which will were counted in the 2025 registration statistics. Three new breeds were recognized in 2026, and will debut in the 2026 registration statistics. Additional breeds are working their way towards recognition through the [AKC Foundation Stock Service](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/foundation-stock-service/) (FSS) and the [Miscellaneous Class](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/miscellaneous-class/). If you’re looking for a puppy of your own, [AKC Marketplace](https://marketplace.akc.org/)can connect you with a responsible breeder.

Knowing your dog will be counted as part of the compilation of the annual breed popularity list is only a small benefit of dog registration. The AKC is the only purebred dog registry in the United States that maintains systematic inspections and investigations. The AKC conducts thousands of inspections each year to ensure compliance with standards that support the welfare, safety, and health of dogs across the nation.

Read on to see the major shifts in popularity, and see where your favorite breed lands!

## The Frenchie Is Four-midable

French Bulldogs have quickly gained popularity over the last decade due to their size and adaptability. They work well in cities and apartments, allowing people with small spaces to have a dog as well.

In 2012, the Frenchie was ranked No. 14 most popular breed, and by 2021, they moved all the way up to the No. 2 spot. [In 2022, they officially moved up](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/most-popular-dog-breeds-2022/) past the Labrador Retriever to take the spot of the Most Popular Breed — a title they’ve held onto for the past four years.

These little dogs hail from France, and [French Bulldog history](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/breed-history-french-bulldog/) is complex. They were recognized by the American Kennel Club in 1898, putting over 100 years of AKC history behind them — and plenty more to come.

## Big Shifts of Popularity for 2025

With 202 breeds in the rankings, 2025 saw some major shifts in breed popularity. Some breeds saw climbs of nearly 30 spots, while others fell in popularity by the same amount. It’s important to note that while some breeds move down in the rankings, it may not mean that they’ve become less popular — it may just mean that another breed has become more popular and moved up.

Some breeds also stayed in the exact same spot, which in most cases means the rankings shifted around it in a way that kept it in the same spot. For example, one breed may be at No. 30 year-over-year, but that could mean that one breed moved up in popularity while another moved down, cancelling out any obvious movement for certain breeds.

### Climbing the Rankings

Some breeds that gained momentum from 2024 to 2025 were working breeds and hunting breeds. The [Bergamasco Sheepdog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bergamasco-sheepdog/), though still towards the bottom of the rankings, went from No. 200 to No. 183, a 17-spot jump. The [English Foxhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/english-foxhound/) and the [Black and Tan Coonhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/black-and-tan-coonhound/) were both up 14 spots, from No. 201 to 187 and No. 151 to 137, respectively. The [English Toy Spaniel](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/english-toy-spaniel/), [Irish Setter](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/irish-setter/), and [Field Spaniel](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/field-spaniel/) all went up 12 spots in the rankings, and the [Greater Swiss Mountain Dog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/greater-swiss-mountain-dog/) and [Norwegian Buhund](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/norwegian-buhund/) were up 11. The [Pointer](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/pointer/) was up 10 spots from No. 121 to 111, and the [Treeing Walker Coonhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/treeing-walker-coonhound/), [Neapolitan Mastiff](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/neapolitan-mastiff/), and [Scottish Deerhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/scottish-deerhound/) were up nine spots from 2024.

The [Wirehaired Viszla](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/wirehaired-vizsla/) saw the highest surge in rankings, going from No. 159 to No. 130, a total of 29 spots. Other notable movements, though smaller, could be attributed to recent trends: the [Giant Schnauzer](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/giant-schnauzer/), which won the AKC National Championship in 2024 and Westminster Best in Show in 2025, saw an increase of five spots from No. 57 to 52.

Other notable jumps include the [American Hairless Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/american-hairless-terrier/), up 17 spots from 125 to 108, and the [Russell Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/russell-terrier/), up 6 from No. 66 to No. 60. The [Otterhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/otterhound/) and [Cirneco dell’Etna](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/cirneco-delletna/), both [rare breeds](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/rarest-dog-breeds-2025/), both moved up seven spots in the rankings, from No. 196 to No. 189 and No. 191 to No. 184. The [Cane Corso](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/cane-corso/) has also been making its way up the rankings over the past few years, rising from No. 14 in 2024 to No. 11 to 2025, nearly breaking into the top 10. [Border Collies](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/border-collie/) rose four spots in the rankings from No. 30 to No. 26, and [Pomeranians](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/pomeranian/) moved up three spots from No. 22 to No. 19.

## New Faces for 2025

The [Danish-Swedish Farmdog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/danish-swedish-farmdog/)[debuted in January 2025](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/danish-swedish-farmdog-newest-akc-recognized-breed/) as a member of the [Working Group](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/working/) — the 202nd AKC-recognized breed. The DSF was included in the rankings for the first time in 2025, debuting at No. 170. The [Lancashire Heeler](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/lancashire-heeler/), which was recognized in January 2024, debuted at No. 189 and moved to No. 190 in 2025.

In January 2026, three new dog breeds were recognized: the [Russian Tsvetnaya Bolonka](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/russian-tsvetnaya-bolonka/), the [Teddy Roosevelt Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/teddy-roosevelt-terrier/), and the [Basset Fauve de Bretagne](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/basset-fauve-de-bretagne/). These three breeds will debut in the 2026 rankings, bringing the total number of AKC-registered breeds to 205.

The American Kennel Club, the world’s largest registry of purebred dogs, uses registration statistics to rank the most popular breeds of the past year. The results for 2025 are in — the [French Bulldog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/french-bulldog/) takes the No. 1 spot once again!

2025 marks the fourth year in a row that the French Bulldog has been able to remain in the top spot. In 2022, they overthrew the [Labrador Retriever](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/labrador-retriever/)‘s [31-year reign](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/most-popular-dog-breeds-of-2021/) in the number one spot, where they’d been since the 1990s. But don’t worry — Labs are still amongst the most popular breeds in the United States.

![Image 104: Young woman sitting in the grass holding her French Bulldog.](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Young-woman-sitting-in-the-grass-holding-her-French-Bulldog.jpg)

Akarawut - stock.adobe.com

The American Kennel Club has recognized 205 breeds since it was first founded in 1884, 202 of which will were counted in the 2025 registration statistics. Three new breeds were recognized in 2026, and will debut in the 2026 registration statistics. Additional breeds are working their way towards recognition through the [AKC Foundation Stock Service](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/foundation-stock-service/) (FSS) and the [Miscellaneous Class](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/miscellaneous-class/). If you’re looking for a puppy of your own, [AKC Marketplace](https://marketplace.akc.org/)can connect you with a responsible breeder.

Knowing your dog will be counted as part of the compilation of the annual breed popularity list is only a small benefit of dog registration. The AKC is the only purebred dog registry in the United States that maintains systematic inspections and investigations. The AKC conducts thousands of inspections each year to ensure compliance with standards that support the welfare, safety, and health of dogs across the nation.

Read on to see the major shifts in popularity, and see where your favorite breed lands!

## The Frenchie Is Four-midable

French Bulldogs have quickly gained popularity over the last decade due to their size and adaptability. They work well in cities and apartments, allowing people with small spaces to have a dog as well.

AKC is a participant in affiliate advertising programs designed to provide a means for sites to earn advertising fees by advertising and linking to akc.org. If you purchase a product through this article, we may receive a portion of the sale.

In 2012, the Frenchie was ranked No. 14 most popular breed, and by 2021, they moved all the way up to the No. 2 spot. [In 2022, they officially moved up](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/most-popular-dog-breeds-2022/) past the Labrador Retriever to take the spot of the Most Popular Breed — a title they’ve held onto for the past four years.

These little dogs hail from France, and [French Bulldog history](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/breed-history-french-bulldog/) is complex. They were recognized by the American Kennel Club in 1898, putting over 100 years of AKC history behind them — and plenty more to come.

## Top 10 Dog Breeds of 2025

The top 10 dog breeds are popular for a reason, and typically don’t shift too much. This year, the top five did see a shift: the [Dachshund](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/dachshund/) moved up in popularity from No. 6 to No. 5, pushing the [Poodle](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/poodle-standard/) out of the top five most popular dog breeds.

1.   French Bulldog
2.   Labrador Retriever
3.   [Golden Retriever](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/golden-retriever/)
4.   [German Shepherd Dog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-shepherd-dog/)
5.   Dachshund
6.   Poodle
7.   [Beagle](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/beagle/)
8.   [Rottweiler](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/rottweiler/)
9.   [German Shorthaired Pointer](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-shorthaired-pointer/)
10.   [Bulldog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bulldog/)

The German Shorthaired Pointer and the Bulldog also switched places from 2024 to 2025. The Bulldog was No. 9 in 2024 and moved to No. 10 for 2025. The GSP did the opposite, rising from No. 10 in 2024 to No. 9 in 2025.

Rottweilers, Beagles, German Shepherd Dogs, Golden Retrievers, Labrador Retrievers, and French Bulldogs all stayed in the same ranking spot year over year.

## Big Shifts of Popularity for 2025

With 202 breeds in the rankings, 2025 saw some major shifts in breed popularity. Some breeds saw climbs of nearly 30 spots, while others fell in popularity by the same amount. It’s important to note that while some breeds move down in the rankings, it may not mean that they’ve become less popular — it may just mean that another breed has become more popular and moved up.

Some breeds also stayed in the exact same spot, which in most cases means the rankings shifted around it in a way that kept it in the same spot. For example, one breed may be at No. 30 year-over-year, but that could mean that one breed moved up in popularity while another moved down, cancelling out any obvious movement for certain breeds.

![Image 108: Danish-Swedish Farmdog standing in a field of grasses and flowers.](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/themes/akc/component-library/assets/img/1x1.trans.gif)

### Climbing the Rankings

Some breeds that gained momentum from 2024 to 2025 were working breeds and hunting breeds. The [Bergamasco Sheepdog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bergamasco-sheepdog/), though still towards the bottom of the rankings, went from No. 200 to No. 183, a 17-spot jump. The [English Foxhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/english-foxhound/) and the [Black and Tan Coonhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/black-and-tan-coonhound/) were both up 14 spots, from No. 201 to 187 and No. 151 to 137, respectively. The [English Toy Spaniel](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/english-toy-spaniel/), [Irish Setter](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/irish-setter/), and [Field Spaniel](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/field-spaniel/) all went up 12 spots in the rankings, and the [Greater Swiss Mountain Dog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/greater-swiss-mountain-dog/) and [Norwegian Buhund](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/norwegian-buhund/) were up 11. The [Pointer](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/pointer/) was up 10 spots from No. 121 to 111, and the [Treeing Walker Coonhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/treeing-walker-coonhound/), [Neapolitan Mastiff](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/neapolitan-mastiff/), and [Scottish Deerhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/scottish-deerhound/) were up nine spots from 2024.

What's a dog breed?

People have been breeding dogs since prehistoric times. The earliest dog breeders used wolves to create domestic dogs. From the beginning, humans purposefully bred dogs to perform various tasks. Hunting, guarding, and herding are thought to be among the earliest jobs eagerly performed by the animal destined to be called “man’s best friend.”

For thousands of years, humans bred dogs toward the physical and mental traits best suited for the work expected of them. The sleek Greyhound types bred to chase fleet-footed prey, and the huge mastiff types used as guard dogs and warriors, are two ancient examples of dogs bred for specific jobs.

As humans became more sophisticated, so did their dogs. Eventually, there emerged specific breeds of dogs, custom-bred to suit the breeders’ local needs and circumstances. The Greyhound, for instance, was the foundation type for the immense Irish Wolfhound and the dainty Italian Greyhound. All three have a distinct family resemblance, but you’d never mistake one for another.

So, then, when is a breed a breed and not just a kind or type of dog? The simplest way to define a breed is to say it always “breeds true.” That is, breeding a purebred Irish Setter to another purebred Irish Setter will always produce dogs instantly recognizable as Irish Setters.

Each breed’s ideal physical traits, movement, and temperament are set down in a written document called a “breed standard.” For example, the breed standard sets forth the traits that make a Cocker Spaniel a Cocker Spaniel and not a Springer Spaniel.

The AKC standard for each breed originates with a “parent club,” the AKC-recognized national club devoted to a particular breed. Once approved by the AKC, a standard becomes both the breeder’s “blueprint” and the instrument used by dog show judges to evaluate a breeder’s work.

There are over 340 dog breeds known throughout the world. The American Kennel Club recognizes 200 breeds. Less

What's a dog breed?

People have been breeding dogs since prehistoric times. The earliest dog breeders used wolves to create domestic dogs. From the beginning, humans purposefully bred dogs to perform various tasks. Hunting, guarding, and herding are thought to be among the earliest jobs eagerly performed by the animal destined to be called “man’s best friend.”

For thousands of years, humans bred dogs toward the physical and mental traits best suited for the work expected of them. The sleek Greyhound types bred to chase fleet-footed prey, and the huge mastiff types used as guard dogs and warriors, are two ancient examples of dogs bred for specific jobs.

As humans became more sophisticated, so did their dogs. Eventually, there emerged specific breeds of dogs, custom-bred to suit the breeders’ local needs and circumstances. The Greyhound, for instance, was the foundation type for the immense Irish Wolfhound and the dainty Italian Greyhound. All three have a distinct family resemblance, but you’d never mistake one for another.

So, then, when is a breed a breed and not just a kind or type of dog? The simplest way to define a breed is to say it always “breeds true.” That is, breeding a purebred Irish Setter to another purebred Irish Setter will always produce dogs instantly recognizable as Irish Setters.

Each breed’s ideal physical traits, movement, and temperament are set down in a written document called a “breed standard.” For example, the breed standard sets forth the traits that make a Cocker Spaniel a Cocker Spaniel and not a Springer Spaniel.

The AKC standard for each breed originates with a “parent club,” the AKC-recognized national club devoted to a particular breed. Once approved by the AKC, a standard becomes both the breeder’s “blueprint” and the instrument used by dog show judges to evaluate a breeder’s work.

There are over 340 dog breeds known throughout the world. The American Kennel Club recognizes 200 breeds. Less

# This Adorable Dog Breed Is Climbing the Ranks in Popularity, According to the AKC

They just became the 5th-most-popular breed in the country.

By [Sarah Vincent](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/author/404949/sarah-vincent/ "Sarah Vincent")Published: May 03, 2026 10:07 AM EDT

Every year, the American Kennel Club puts out a list ranking the popularity of every dog breed. It’s a fun annual snapshot of what’s hot in the canine world, based on how many dogs are registered as each kind of breed.

While the top 10 dog breeds commonly stay the same year over year (the lab was the top dog in America for 31 years straight!), sometimes there are surprising shifts. In the 2025 rankings, one particularly adorable dog breed is working its way up the popularity list, breaking into the top 5.

The lucky dog is, drumroll please…the Dachshund!

## More Pets

*   [![Image 21](https://hips.hearstapps.com/hmg-prod/images/dog-puppy-on-garden-royalty-free-image-1586966191.jpg?crop=0.752xw:1.00xh;0.175xw,0&resize=300:*)The 40 Cutest Dog Breeds](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/relationships/pets/g4531/cutest-dog-breeds-converted/)
*   [![Image 22](https://hips.hearstapps.com/hmg-prod/images/dog-strollers-6888e244d5068.png?crop=0.502xw:1.00xh;0.250xw,0&resize=300:*)Our Favorite Dog Strollers for Pups of All Sizes](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/life/pets/g41577207/best-dog-strollers-converted/)

These long, wiggly dogs are known for their small bodies but big personalities. Their undeniable charm and adorably comic looks have made them increasingly popular, especially on social media. Pet owners agree that their floppy ears and stumpy legs are too cute to pass up, pushing Dachshunds back into one of the top spots for popularity.

The last time the Dachshund was in the top 5 most popular dog breeds was in 2003. After that point, the [small dog breed's](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/life/pets/advice/g1754/small-dog-breeds/) popularity declined until it finally dropped out of the top 10 in 2014. Dachshunds fell as far as #13 in the rankings from 2015 to 2017 before slowly climbing in popularity again in recent years. Now they are once again one of the top dogs, dethroning the poodle to take #5 on the popularity list.

However, both dogs rank behind the number one winner: the French Bulldog.

Frenchies have been crowned the most popular dog breed in America for the fourth year in a row! They first took the title in 2022 and have held strong at the top ever since. Dog lovers just can’t get enough of their adaptable nature, playful energy, and iconic bat ears.

This is the full list of the top 10 most popular dog breeds in 2025:

1.   French Bulldog
2.   Labrador Retriever
3.   Golden Retriever
4.   German Shepherd Dog
5.   Dachshund
6.   Poodle
7.   Beagle
8.   Rottweiler
9.   German Shorthaired Pointer
10.   Bulldog

Will the French Bulldog continue to reign supreme next year, or will the Dachshund keep climbing the ranks to eventually become the most popular dog breed in America?

We can’t wait to find out.

# This Adorable Dog Breed Is Climbing the Ranks in Popularity, According to the AKC

They just became the 5th-most-popular breed in the country.

By [Sarah Vincent](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/author/404949/sarah-vincent/ "Sarah Vincent")Published: May 03, 2026 10:07 AM EDT

Every year, the American Kennel Club puts out a list ranking the popularity of every dog breed. It’s a fun annual snapshot of what’s hot in the canine world, based on how many dogs are registered as each kind of breed.

While the top 10 dog breeds commonly stay the same year over year (the lab was the top dog in America for 31 years straight!), sometimes there are surprising shifts. In the 2025 rankings, one particularly adorable dog breed is working its way up the popularity list, breaking into the top 5.

The lucky dog is, drumroll please…the Dachshund!

## More Pets

*   [![Image 21](https://hips.hearstapps.com/hmg-prod/images/dog-puppy-on-garden-royalty-free-image-1586966191.jpg?crop=0.752xw:1.00xh;0.175xw,0&resize=300:*)The 40 Cutest Dog Breeds](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/relationships/pets/g4531/cutest-dog-breeds-converted/)
*   [![Image 22](https://hips.hearstapps.com/hmg-prod/images/dog-strollers-6888e244d5068.png?crop=0.502xw:1.00xh;0.250xw,0&resize=300:*)Our Favorite Dog Strollers for Pups of All Sizes](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/life/pets/g41577207/best-dog-strollers-converted/)

These long, wiggly dogs are known for their small bodies but big personalities. Their undeniable charm and adorably comic looks have made them increasingly popular, especially on social media. Pet owners agree that their floppy ears and stumpy legs are too cute to pass up, pushing Dachshunds back into one of the top spots for popularity.

The last time the Dachshund was in the top 5 most popular dog breeds was in 2003. After that point, the [small dog breed's](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/life/pets/advice/g1754/small-dog-breeds/) popularity declined until it finally dropped out of the top 10 in 2014. Dachshunds fell as far as #13 in the rankings from 2015 to 2017 before slowly climbing in popularity again in recent years. Now they are once again one of the top dogs, dethroning the poodle to take #5 on the popularity list.

However, both dogs rank behind the number one winner: the French Bulldog.

Frenchies have been crowned the most popular dog breed in America for the fourth year in a row! They first took the title in 2022 and have held strong at the top ever since. Dog lovers just can’t get enough of their adaptable nature, playful energy, and iconic bat ears.

This is the full list of the top 10 most popular dog breeds in 2025:

1.   French Bulldog
2.   Labrador Retriever
3.   Golden Retriever
4.   German Shepherd Dog
5.   Dachshund
6.   Poodle
7.   Beagle
8.   Rottweiler
9.   German Shorthaired Pointer
10.   Bulldog

Will the French Bulldog continue to reign supreme next year, or will the Dachshund keep climbing the ranks to eventually become the most popular dog breed in America?

We can’t wait to find out.

Labrador retrievers revealed as the most popular dog breed in 2017 

By ABC News

March 28, 2018, 1:01 PM

*     

Labrador retrievers are the most popular dog breed in the United States, but perhaps not for long.

The French bulldog could soon take their place on the American Kennel Club (AKC)’s annual list of most popular dog breeds.

The French bulldog climbed into the top four last year, knocking the Beagle out of the top five for the first time in nearly 20 years.

The 2017 list was released today by the AKC.

“The French bulldog is poised for a takeover,” AKC Executive Secretary Gina DiNardo said in a statement, noting the breed’s “adaptability” and “loveable temperament.”

The Labrador retriever though has held the top ranking in AKC’s list for 27 years, a feat DiNardo attributed to the breed’s versatility and family-friendly nature.

Labrador retrievers revealed as the most popular dog breed in 2017 

By ABC News

March 28, 2018, 1:01 PM

*     

Labrador retrievers are the most popular dog breed in the United States, but perhaps not for long.

The French bulldog could soon take their place on the American Kennel Club (AKC)’s annual list of most popular dog breeds.

The French bulldog climbed into the top four last year, knocking the Beagle out of the top five for the first time in nearly 20 years.

The 2017 list was released today by the AKC.

“The French bulldog is poised for a takeover,” AKC Executive Secretary Gina DiNardo said in a statement, noting the breed’s “adaptability” and “loveable temperament.”

The Labrador retriever though has held the top ranking in AKC’s list for 27 years, a feat DiNardo attributed to the breed’s versatility and family-friendly nature.

![Image 5](https://s.abcnews.com/images/Lifestyle/labrador-retriever-gty-hb-180327_hpMain.jpg)

Every year the [American Kennel Club](http://akc.org/) releases our ranking of the most popular dog breeds based on AKC registration statistics for the previous year.

The [French Bulldog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/french-bulldog/) continues to top the rankings at the No. 1 spot for the fourth year in a row. The [Labrador Retriever](https://www.akc.org/press-releases/labrador-retriever-celebrates-30-years-top-spot-french-bulldog-overtakes-german-shepherd-dog-number-2-spot/), who had a 31-year run as the most popular breed, is in the No. 2 spot for the third year in a row. In 2025, the Poodle moved out of the top five, replaced by the [Dachshund](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/dachshund/). Many other breeds have moved spots from 2024 to 2025. Every year the [American Kennel Club](http://akc.org/) releases our ranking of the most popular dog breeds based on AKC registration statistics for the previous year.

The [French Bulldog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/french-bulldog/) continues to top the rankings at the No. 1 spot for the fourth year in a row. The [Labrador Retriever](https://www.akc.org/press-releases/labrador-retriever-celebrates-30-years-top-spot-french-bulldog-overtakes-german-shepherd-dog-number-2-spot/), who had a 31-year run as the most popular breed, is in the No. 2 spot for the third year in a row. In 2025, the Poodle moved out of the top five, replaced by the [Dachshund](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/dachshund/). Many other breeds have moved spots from 2024 to 2025. Below, find ranked annual lists of AKC-recognized breeds.

The American Kennel Club, the world’s largest registry of purebred dogs, uses registration statistics to rank the most popular breeds of the past year. The results for 2025 are in — the [French Bulldog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/french-bulldog/) takes the No. 1 spot once again!

2025 marks the fourth year in a row that the French Bulldog has been able to remain in the top spot. In 2022, they overthrew the [Labrador Retriever](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/labrador-retriever/)‘s [31-year reign](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/most-popular-dog-breeds-of-2021/) in the number one spot, where they’d been since the 1990s. But don’t worry — Labs are still amongst the most popular breeds in the United States.

![Image 104: Young woman sitting in the grass holding her French Bulldog.](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Young-woman-sitting-in-the-grass-holding-her-French-Bulldog.jpg)

Akarawut - stock.adobe.com

The American Kennel Club has recognized 205 breeds since it was first founded in 1884, 202 of which will were counted in the 2025 registration statistics. Three new breeds were recognized in 2026, and will debut in the 2026 registration statistics. Additional breeds are working their way towards recognition through the [AKC Foundation Stock Service](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/foundation-stock-service/) (FSS) and the [Miscellaneous Class](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/miscellaneous-class/). If you’re looking for a puppy of your own, [AKC Marketplace](https://marketplace.akc.org/)can connect you with a responsible breeder.

Knowing your dog will be counted as part of the compilation of the annual breed popularity list is only a small benefit of dog registration. The AKC is the only purebred dog registry in the United States that maintains systematic inspections and investigations. The AKC conducts thousands of inspections each year to ensure compliance with standards that support the welfare, safety, and health of dogs across the nation.

Read on to see the major shifts in popularity, and see where your favorite breed lands!

## The Frenchie Is Four-midable

French Bulldogs have quickly gained popularity over the last decade due to their size and adaptability. They work well in cities and apartments, allowing people with small spaces to have a dog as well.

In 2012, the Frenchie was ranked No. 14 most popular breed, and by 2021, they moved all the way up to the No. 2 spot. [In 2022, they officially moved up](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/most-popular-dog-breeds-2022/) past the Labrador Retriever to take the spot of the Most Popular Breed — a title they’ve held onto for the past four years.

These little dogs hail from France, and [French Bulldog history](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/breed-history-french-bulldog/) is complex. They were recognized by the American Kennel Club in 1898, putting over 100 years of AKC history behind them — and plenty more to come.

The top 10 dog breeds are popular for a reason, and typically don’t shift too much. This year, the top five did see a shift: the [Dachshund](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/dachshund/) moved up in popularity from No. 6 to No. 5, pushing the [Poodle](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/poodle-standard/) out of the top five most popular dog breeds.

The German Shorthaired Pointer and the Bulldog also switched places from 2024 to 2025. The Bulldog was No. 9 in 2024 and moved to No. 10 for 2025. The GSP did the opposite, rising from No. 10 in 2024 to No. 9 in 2025.

Rottweilers, Beagles, German Shepherd Dogs, Golden Retrievers, Labrador Retrievers, and French Bulldogs all stayed in the same ranking spot year over year.

## Big Shifts of Popularity for 2025

With 202 breeds in the rankings, 2025 saw some major shifts in breed popularity. Some breeds saw climbs of nearly 30 spots, while others fell in popularity by the same amount. It’s important to note that while some breeds move down in the rankings, it may not mean that they’ve become less popular — it may just mean that another breed has become more popular and moved up.

Some breeds also stayed in the exact same spot, which in most cases means the rankings shifted around it in a way that kept it in the same spot. For example, one breed may be at No. 30 year-over-year, but that could mean that one breed moved up in popularity while another moved down, cancelling out any obvious movement for certain breeds.

![Image 108: Danish-Swedish Farmdog standing in a field of grasses and flowers.](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/themes/akc/component-library/assets/img/1x1.trans.gif)

Shakarrigrafie via Shutterstock

### Climbing the Rankings

Some breeds that gained momentum from 2024 to 2025 were working breeds and hunting breeds. The [Bergamasco Sheepdog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bergamasco-sheepdog/), though still towards the bottom of the rankings, went from No. 200 to No. 183, a 17-spot jump. The [English Foxhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/english-foxhound/) and the [Black and Tan Coonhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/black-and-tan-coonhound/) were both up 14 spots, from No. 201 to 187 and No. 151 to 137, respectively. The [English Toy Spaniel](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/english-toy-spaniel/), [Irish Setter](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/irish-setter/), and [Field Spaniel](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/field-spaniel/) all went up 12 spots in the rankings, and the [Greater Swiss Mountain Dog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/greater-swiss-mountain-dog/) and [Norwegian Buhund](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/norwegian-buhund/) were up 11. The [Pointer](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/pointer/) was up 10 spots from No. 121 to 111, and the [Treeing Walker Coonhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/treeing-walker-coonhound/), [Neapolitan Mastiff](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/neapolitan-mastiff/), and [Scottish Deerhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/scottish-deerhound/) were up nine spots from 2024.

The [Wirehaired Viszla](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/wirehaired-vizsla/) saw the highest surge in rankings, going from No. 159 to No. 130, a total of 29 spots. Other notable movements, though smaller, could be attributed to recent trends: the [Giant Schnauzer](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/giant-schnauzer/), which won the AKC National Championship in 2024 and Westminster Best in Show in 2025, saw an increase of five spots from No. 57 to 52.

Other notable jumps include the [American Hairless Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/american-hairless-terrier/), up 17 spots from 125 to 108, and the [Russell Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/russell-terrier/), up 6 from No. 66 to No. 60. The [Otterhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/otterhound/) and [Cirneco dell’Etna](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/cirneco-delletna/), both [rare breeds](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/rarest-dog-breeds-2025/), both moved up seven spots in the rankings, from No. 196 to No. 189 and No. 191 to No. 184. The [Cane Corso](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/cane-corso/) has also been making its way up the rankings over the past few years, rising from No. 14 in 2024 to No. 11 to 2025, nearly breaking into the top 10. [Border Collies](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/border-collie/) rose four spots in the rankings from No. 30 to No. 26, and [Pomeranians](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/pomeranian/) moved up three spots from No. 22 to No. 19.

### Moving Down on the List

![Image 110: Danish-Swedish Farmdog standing in a field of grasses and flowers.](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/themes/akc/component-library/assets/img/1x1.trans.gif)

Ekaterina Krivtsova/Shutterstock

Similar to climbs in the rankings, shifts down don’t always mean a breed becomes less popular than the year prior. It could also just mean that a great deal has shifted around it, causing it to go further down in the rankings. The biggest shifts in rankings were the [Greyhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/greyhound/), down 33 from No. 188 to No. 151, and the [Briard](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/briard/) and [Black Russian Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/black-russian-terrier/), both down 27 spots from 2024. The [Kerry Blue Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/kerry-blue-terrier/), which rose 25 spots from No. 160 to No. 135 in 2024, went to No. 155 in 2025, down 20 spots.

Some popular breeds that moved down in the rankings: the [Miniature American Shepherd](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/miniature-american-shepherd/) went from No. 24 to No. 28, the [Siberian Husky](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/siberian-husky/) went from No. 26 to No. 30, the [West Highland White Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/west-highland-white-terrier/) went from No. 41 to No. 45, and the [Chesapeake Bay Retriever](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/chesapeake-bay-retriever/) went from No. 56 to No. 52.

### Holding Their Spots

Breeds that may have seen few gains or losses, or may have remained in the same spot due to the sum of other breeds’ gains and losses, are also of note. The [Boston Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/boston-terrier/) has sat comfortably at No. 23 since 2023, as has the [Havanese](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/havanese/) at No. 25, and the [Basset Hound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/basset-hound/) at No. 34. Also unwavering in their placements were the [Maltese](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/maltese/) at No. 27 and the [Finnish Spitz](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/finnish-spitz/) at No. 194.

## New Faces for 2025

The [Danish-Swedish Farmdog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/danish-swedish-farmdog/)[debuted in January 2025](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/danish-swedish-farmdog-newest-akc-recognized-breed/) as a member of the [Working Group](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/working/) — the 202nd AKC-recognized breed. The DSF was included in the rankings for the first time in 2025, debuting at No. 170. The [Lancashire Heeler](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/lancashire-heeler/), which was recognized in January 2024, debuted at No. 189 and moved to No. 190 in 2025.

In January 2026, three new dog breeds were recognized: the [Russian Tsvetnaya Bolonka](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/russian-tsvetnaya-bolonka/), the [Teddy Roosevelt Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/teddy-roosevelt-terrier/), and the [Basset Fauve de Bretagne](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/basset-fauve-de-bretagne/). These three breeds will debut in the 2026 rankings, bringing the total number of AKC-registered breeds to 205.

The American Kennel Club, the world’s largest registry of purebred dogs, uses registration statistics to rank the most popular breeds of the past year. The results for 2025 are in — the [French Bulldog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/french-bulldog/) takes the No. 1 spot once again!

2025 marks the fourth year in a row that the French Bulldog has been able to remain in the top spot. In 2022, they overthrew the [Labrador Retriever](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/labrador-retriever/)‘s [31-year reign](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/most-popular-dog-breeds-of-2021/) in the number one spot, where they’d been since the 1990s. But don’t worry — Labs are still amongst the most popular breeds in the United States.

![Image 104: Young woman sitting in the grass holding her French Bulldog.](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Young-woman-sitting-in-the-grass-holding-her-French-Bulldog.jpg)

Akarawut - stock.adobe.com

The American Kennel Club has recognized 205 breeds since it was first founded in 1884, 202 of which will were counted in the 2025 registration statistics. Three new breeds were recognized in 2026, and will debut in the 2026 registration statistics. Additional breeds are working their way towards recognition through the [AKC Foundation Stock Service](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/foundation-stock-service/) (FSS) and the [Miscellaneous Class](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/miscellaneous-class/). If you’re looking for a puppy of your own, [AKC Marketplace](https://marketplace.akc.org/)can connect you with a responsible breeder.

Knowing your dog will be counted as part of the compilation of the annual breed popularity list is only a small benefit of dog registration. The AKC is the only purebred dog registry in the United States that maintains systematic inspections and investigations. The AKC conducts thousands of inspections each year to ensure compliance with standards that support the welfare, safety, and health of dogs across the nation.

Read on to see the major shifts in popularity, and see where your favorite breed lands!

## The Frenchie Is Four-midable

French Bulldogs have quickly gained popularity over the last decade due to their size and adaptability. They work well in cities and apartments, allowing people with small spaces to have a dog as well.

In 2012, the Frenchie was ranked No. 14 most popular breed, and by 2021, they moved all the way up to the No. 2 spot. [In 2022, they officially moved up](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/most-popular-dog-breeds-2022/) past the Labrador Retriever to take the spot of the Most Popular Breed — a title they’ve held onto for the past four years.

These little dogs hail from France, and [French Bulldog history](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/breed-history-french-bulldog/) is complex. They were recognized by the American Kennel Club in 1898, putting over 100 years of AKC history behind them — and plenty more to come.

## Big Shifts of Popularity for 2025

With 202 breeds in the rankings, 2025 saw some major shifts in breed popularity. Some breeds saw climbs of nearly 30 spots, while others fell in popularity by the same amount. It’s important to note that while some breeds move down in the rankings, it may not mean that they’ve become less popular — it may just mean that another breed has become more popular and moved up.

Some breeds also stayed in the exact same spot, which in most cases means the rankings shifted around it in a way that kept it in the same spot. For example, one breed may be at No. 30 year-over-year, but that could mean that one breed moved up in popularity while another moved down, cancelling out any obvious movement for certain breeds.

### Climbing the Rankings

Some breeds that gained momentum from 2024 to 2025 were working breeds and hunting breeds. The [Bergamasco Sheepdog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bergamasco-sheepdog/), though still towards the bottom of the rankings, went from No. 200 to No. 183, a 17-spot jump. The [English Foxhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/english-foxhound/) and the [Black and Tan Coonhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/black-and-tan-coonhound/) were both up 14 spots, from No. 201 to 187 and No. 151 to 137, respectively. The [English Toy Spaniel](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/english-toy-spaniel/), [Irish Setter](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/irish-setter/), and [Field Spaniel](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/field-spaniel/) all went up 12 spots in the rankings, and the [Greater Swiss Mountain Dog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/greater-swiss-mountain-dog/) and [Norwegian Buhund](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/norwegian-buhund/) were up 11. The [Pointer](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/pointer/) was up 10 spots from No. 121 to 111, and the [Treeing Walker Coonhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/treeing-walker-coonhound/), [Neapolitan Mastiff](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/neapolitan-mastiff/), and [Scottish Deerhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/scottish-deerhound/) were up nine spots from 2024.

The [Wirehaired Viszla](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/wirehaired-vizsla/) saw the highest surge in rankings, going from No. 159 to No. 130, a total of 29 spots. Other notable movements, though smaller, could be attributed to recent trends: the [Giant Schnauzer](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/giant-schnauzer/), which won the AKC National Championship in 2024 and Westminster Best in Show in 2025, saw an increase of five spots from No. 57 to 52.

Other notable jumps include the [American Hairless Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/american-hairless-terrier/), up 17 spots from 125 to 108, and the [Russell Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/russell-terrier/), up 6 from No. 66 to No. 60. The [Otterhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/otterhound/) and [Cirneco dell’Etna](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/cirneco-delletna/), both [rare breeds](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/rarest-dog-breeds-2025/), both moved up seven spots in the rankings, from No. 196 to No. 189 and No. 191 to No. 184. The [Cane Corso](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/cane-corso/) has also been making its way up the rankings over the past few years, rising from No. 14 in 2024 to No. 11 to 2025, nearly breaking into the top 10. [Border Collies](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/border-collie/) rose four spots in the rankings from No. 30 to No. 26, and [Pomeranians](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/pomeranian/) moved up three spots from No. 22 to No. 19.

## New Faces for 2025

The [Danish-Swedish Farmdog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/danish-swedish-farmdog/)[debuted in January 2025](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/danish-swedish-farmdog-newest-akc-recognized-breed/) as a member of the [Working Group](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/working/) — the 202nd AKC-recognized breed. The DSF was included in the rankings for the first time in 2025, debuting at No. 170. The [Lancashire Heeler](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/lancashire-heeler/), which was recognized in January 2024, debuted at No. 189 and moved to No. 190 in 2025.

In January 2026, three new dog breeds were recognized: the [Russian Tsvetnaya Bolonka](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/russian-tsvetnaya-bolonka/), the [Teddy Roosevelt Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/teddy-roosevelt-terrier/), and the [Basset Fauve de Bretagne](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/basset-fauve-de-bretagne/). These three breeds will debut in the 2026 rankings, bringing the total number of AKC-registered breeds to 205.

As the world’s largest registry of purebred dogs, the AKC uses our registration statistics to rank the most popular breeds of the past year — and the numbers are in!

The [French Bulldog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/french-bulldog/) has secured the No. 1 spot as the most popular dog breed in the United States for the third year in a row. In 2022, the Frenchie took the Most Popular title from the [Labrador Retriever,](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/labrador-retriever/) a breed who had previously sat comfortably at [No. 1 for 31 years](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/most-popular-dog-breeds-of-2021/).

## Staying in the No.1 Spot

French Bulldogs have surged to the top, quickly amassing popularity for their size and adaptability. It’s hard to miss their signature bat ears on city streets and rural roads alike.

Over the last 12 years, they’ve climbed the rankings. In 2012, they were ranked the No. 14 most popular breed, and by 2021, they’d made it to the No. 2 spot. They officially became the [No.1 breed in 2022](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/most-popular-dog-breeds-2022/), and have held that title for three years now.

French Bulldogs are especially popular in cities, but their playful nature and compact size are great for a variety of lifestyles. These little dogs originated in France, and [French Bulldog history](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/breed-history-french-bulldog/) is complex. They were recognized by the American Kennel Club in 1898, and now have over 100 years of AKC history behind them.

![Image 103: French Bulldog giving a kiss to another French Bulldog on the couch.](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/12/French-Bulldog-giving-a-kiss-to-another-French-Bulldog-on-the-couch.jpg)

©fotosmile777 - stock.adobe.com

## Top 10 Dog Breeds of 2024

The top five and top 10 dog breeds are popular for a reason, and typically don’t shift too much. The Frenchie is again at No. 1, followed by the Labrador Retriever, [Golden Retriever](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/golden-retriever/), [German Shepherd Dog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-shepherd-dog/), and [Poodle](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/poodle-standard/) at No. 5.

As for the rest of the top 10, a few placements have shifted. [Beagles](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/beagle/) have moved from No. 8 to No. 7, moving [Bulldogs](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bulldog/) from No. 7 to No. 9 and [Rottweilers](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/rottweiler/) from No. 9 to No. 8. [German Shorthaired Pointers](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-shorthaired-pointer/) remain at No. 10 from 2023 to 2024.

## Big Shifts of Note in 2024

2024 saw major shifts for a lot of breeds across the rankings. While some breeds surged over 20 rankings higher, others shifted 10 or more rankings lower. Many breeds, especially in the 20s and 30s, stayed at the same spot from 2023 to 2024.

The [Danish-Swedish Farmdog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/danish-swedish-farmdog/), which [debuted in January 2025](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/danish-swedish-farmdog-newest-akc-recognized-breed/) as part of the [Working Group](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/working/) as the 202nd AKC-recognized breed will be included in the registration rankings for 2025. The Lancashire Heeler, which became AKC-recognized in January 2024, debuted in the 2024 rankings at No. 189.

![Image 105: English Foxhound standing in a field with a pack.](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/themes/akc/component-library/assets/img/1x1.trans.gif)

Kewalin Madsen/Shutterstock

### Climbing the Rankings

The biggest surges in popularity among breeds came from four very different dog breeds. The [Kerry Blue Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/kerry-blue-terrier/) had the highest jump, moving up a whopping 25 spots from No. 160 to No. 135. The [Bracco Italiano](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bracco-italiano/), [recognized by the AKC in 2022](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/bracco-italiano-becomes-newest-akc-recognized-dog-breed-in-2022/), continues to move up. From 2023 to 2024, the Bracco moved up 20 spots from No. 152 to No. 132.

The [German Pinscher](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-pinscher/) and the [American Staffordshire Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/american-staffordshire-terrier/) both went up 18 spots year over year. The German Pinscher moved from No. 151 to No. 133, and the AmStaff moved from No. 95 to No. 77.

The [Bedlington Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bedlington-terrier/) went up 15 ranks from No. 149 to No. 134, and the[Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/nova-scotia-duck-tolling-retriever/) went up 14 rankings from No. 83 to No. 69.

The [Brussels Griffon](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/brussels-griffon/), [American Eskimo Dog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/american-eskimo-dog/), and [Harrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/harrier/) all went up 13 placements. The Brussels Griffon moved from No. 92 to No. 84, the Eskie from No. 129 to No. 116, and the Harrier from No. 190 to No. 183.

The [Mudi](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/mudi/), [recognized in 2022](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/mudi-becomes-newest-akc-recognized-dog-breed-in-2022/), continues to climb the ranks, going up 12 from No. 130 in 2023 to No. 122 in 2024. The [Polish Lowland Sheepdog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/polish-lowland-sheepdog/) also went up 12 spots, from No. 193 to No. 181.

The [Manchester Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/manchester-terrier-standard/) went up 11 ranks from No. 126 to No. 115, and the [Boykin Spaniel](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/boykin-spaniel/) went up 10 rankings from No. 75 to No. 65.

### Moving Down on the List

![Image 107: English Foxhound standing in a field with a pack.](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/themes/akc/component-library/assets/img/1x1.trans.gif)

©Angel Sallade Photog - stock.adobe.com

The [Saluki](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/saluki/), [Black and Tan Coonhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/black-and-tan-coonhound/), and [Wirehaired Vizsla](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/wirehaired-vizsla/) all saw their breeds move down the list significantly from 2023 to 2024. The Saluki went from No. 120 to No. 141, down 21 spots. The Black and Tan Coonhound went down 20 spots, from No. 131 to No. 151. Down 17 from 2023 to 2024, the Wirehaired Vizsla went from the No. 142 spot to No. 159.

The [Chinese Shar-Pei](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/chinese-shar-pei/) went from No. 70 to No. 83, down 13 spots. Also down 13 spots was the [Field Spaniel](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/field-spaniel/), from No. 147 to No. 160.

Each down 12 spots were the [Bergamasco Sheepdog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bergamasco-sheepdog/), the [Old English Sheepdog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/old-english-sheepdog/), and the [Dogue de Bordeaux](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/dogue-de-bordeaux/). They went from No. 188 to No. 200, No. 77 to No. 89, and No. 84 to No. 96 respectfully.

Other big dogs have moved down as well. The [Neapolitan Mastiff](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/neapolitan-mastiff/) and [Great Pyrenees](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/great-pyrenees/) are both down 10 spots. The Neapolitan Mastiff went from No. 118 to No. 128, and the Pyr went from No. 64 to No. 74.

### Holding Their Spots

These breeds found solace in their 2023 placements and stayed there. The top five breeds stayed the same, but so did the [Shih Tzu](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/shih-tzu/) at No. 20, [Pomeranian](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/pomeranian/) at No. 22, [Boston Terrier](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/boston-terrier/) at No. 23, and [Havanese](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/havanese/) at No. 25. In the 30s, [Belgian Malinois](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/belgian-malinois/) stayed at No. 33, [Basset Hounds](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/basset-hound/) stayed at No. 34, [Vizsla](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/vizsla/) stayed at No. 35, and the [Maltese](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/maltese/) stayed at No. 37. The [German Wirehaired Pointer](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-wirehaired-pointer/) stayed at No. 61, and the [Chow Chow](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/chow-chow/) stayed at No. 88. The [Finnish Spitz](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/finnish-spitz/) kept their spot at No. 194.

## Least Popular Dog Breeds of 2024

Often rare breeds, the dogs in the bottom 20 have the lowest numbers in terms of registration in the United States. There are 201 breeds counted since the addition of the [Lancashire Heeler](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/lancashire-heeler/) in 2024, and there will be 202 for 2025 when the registration numbers for the Danish-Swedish Farmdog are added.

The [Sloughi](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/sloughi/), which was ranked last at No. 200 in 2023, has made the jump to No. 197 in 2024. They’re followed by the [Norwegian Lundehund](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/lancashire-heeler/) at No. 198, the [Grand Basset Griffon Vendeen](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/grand-basset-griffon-vendeen/) at No. 199, the [Bergamasco Sheepdog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/bergamasco-sheepdog/) at No. 200, and the [English Foxhound](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/english-foxhound/) at No. 201. The English Foxhound was ranked 199 in 2023, and dropped two spots in 2024.

![Image 109: English Foxhound standing in a field with a pack.](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/themes/akc/component-library/assets/img/1x1.trans.gif)

Chris Strickland/Getty Images Plus via Getty Images

The American Kennel Club has recognized 202 breeds since it was first founded in 1884, with additional breeds working their way towards recognition through the [AKC Foundation Stock Service](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/foundation-stock-service/) (FSS) and the [Miscellaneous Class](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/miscellaneous-class/). If you’re looking for a puppy of your own, [AKC Marketplace](https://marketplace.akc.org/)can connect you with a responsible breeder.

As the world’s largest registry of purebred dogs, the AKC uses our registration statistics to rank the most popular breeds of the past year — and the numbers are in!

The [French Bulldog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/french-bulldog/) has secured the No. 1 spot as the most popular dog breed in the United States for the third year in a row. In 2022, the Frenchie took the Most Popular title from the [Labrador Retriever,](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/labrador-retriever/) a breed who had previously sat comfortably at [No. 1 for 31 years](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/most-popular-dog-breeds-of-2021/).

## Staying in the No.1 Spot

French Bulldogs have surged to the top, quickly amassing popularity for their size and adaptability. It’s hard to miss their signature bat ears on city streets and rural roads alike.

Over the last 12 years, they’ve climbed the rankings. In 2012, they were ranked the No. 14 most popular breed, and by 2021, they’d made it to the No. 2 spot. They officially became the [No.1 breed in 2022](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/most-popular-dog-breeds-2022/), and have held that title for three years now.

French Bulldogs are especially popular in cities, but their playful nature and compact size are great for a variety of lifestyles. These little dogs originated in France, and [French Bulldog history](https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/dog-breeds/breed-history-french-bulldog/) is complex. They were recognized by the American Kennel Club in 1898, and now have over 100 years of AKC history behind them.

![Image 103: French Bulldog giving a kiss to another French Bulldog on the couch.](https://www.akc.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/12/French-Bulldog-giving-a-kiss-to-another-French-Bulldog-on-the-couch.jpg)

©fotosmile777 - stock.adobe.com

## Top 10 Dog Breeds of 2024

The top five and top 10 dog breeds are popular for a reason, and typically don’t shift too much. The Frenchie is again at No. 1, followed by the Labrador Retriever, [Golden Retriever](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/golden-retriever/), [German Shepherd Dog](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/german-shepherd-dog/), and [Poodle](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/poodle-standard/) at No. 5.
